1: # LANGSPEC C2 — Class/Method Rules (26) — Plan
2: 
3: **Module:** `crates/mlt_rules/src/language_spec.rs` — LanguageSpecEngine. All checks gated by `is_check_enabled`, dispatched in `check_class_rules` (has `class: &ClassMeta`).
4: 
5: ## Checks & official messages (all Error)
6: | ID | Message |
7: |----|---------|
8: | MABSEAC | Instance properties and methods are illegal in classes that are both Sealed and Abstract. |
9: | MABSEAM | A method cannot be both Abstract and Sealed. |
10: | MCAPP | Private property cannot be Abstract. |
11: | MCCBS | A superclass constructor is being called, but VAR_NAME is not a declared superclass name. |
12: | MCCBU | This superclass constructor is called after a use of the constructed object. |
13: | MCCMC | Constructor for superclass can only be called once. |
14: | MCCSOP | Unable to modify Constant property VAR_NAME. |
15: | MCGSA | Method VAR_NAME tries to set or get an abstract property. |
16: | MCMIO | Method has too many inputs or outputs. |
17: | MCMSP | Private method cannot be Abstract. |
18: | MCMTP | TestParameterDefinition methods must be Static. |
19: | MCPIN | Unable to initialize class property to an instance of the class itself. |
20: | MCPSG | Set or get method must be fully defined in the class definition file. |
21: | MCSCC | To call the superclass constructor, the subclass constructor name must match the subclass name. |
22: | MCSCF | A superclass constructor must be assigned to the first constructor output argument. |
23: | MCSCM | To call a superclass method, the method name must match the subclass method name. |
24: | MCSCN | Method VAR_NAME tries to set a constant property. |
25: | MCSCO | A superclass constructor must be called using the first constructor output argument. |
26: | MCSCT | Superclass constructor call must not be conditionalized or be part of another expression. |
27: | MCSMO | Returning multiple outputs from a superclass object initialization is not supported. |
28: | MCSWA | A sealed class cannot specify allowed subclasses. |
29: | MTAGS3 | Cannot use the Access attribute when using the SetAccess or GetAccess attribute. |
30: | MTMAT | Attribute can only be set once. |
31: | MWKCL | A WeakHandle property must restrict its type using a class validation. |
32: | MWKCT | Specifying both WeakHandle and Constant attributes on the same property is not supported. |
33: | MWKREF | Specifying both WeakHandle and Dependent attributes is invalid. |
34: 
35: ## Existing infrastructure (reuse!)
36: `check_class_rules` already calls: MCFIL, MCDIR, MCRED, MCCBD, setter/getter signatures, MCEB, MCANI, MCASC, MCSGA, MCSGP. New checks slot into the same function. `ClassMeta` provides: name, superclasses, attributes (Vec<AttributeMeta>), properties_blocks (Vec<PropertiesBlockMeta> with attributes + properties), methods_blocks (Vec<MethodsBlockMeta> with attributes + methods: Vec<FunctionMeta>).
37: 
38: ## Detection (grouped by pattern)
39: 
40: ### A. Attribute conflicts (class-level, no tree walk)
41: Using `ClassMeta.attributes`:
42: - Sealed AND Abstract → MABSEAC (check properties_blocks/methods_blocks for instance members)
43: - Sealed + `AllowedSubclasses` specified → MCSWA
44: - Attribute appears twice → MTMAT (scan duplicate attribute names)
45: - `Access` alongside `SetAccess`/`GetAccess` → MTAGS3 (check properties/methods block attributes)
46: 
47: ### B. Abstract/Sealed method & property rules (methods_blocks + properties_blocks)
48: - Method both Abstract and Sealed → MABSEAM
49: - Private method Abstract → MCMSP
50: - Private property Abstract → MCAPP
51: - Set/get method tries to access abstract property → MCGSA (needs property-name matching)
52: - Set/get method not fully defined in file → MCPSG
53: 
54: ### C. Constant property rules
55: - Assigning to Constant property → MCCSOP
56: - Method tries to set constant property → MCSCN
57: 
58: ### D. WeakHandle property rules (properties_blocks)
59: - WeakHandle property without class validation (no type_constraint) → MWKCL
60: - WeakHandle + Constant → MWKCT
61: - WeakHandle + Dependent → MWKREF
62: 
63: ### E. Constructor/superclass rules (methods_blocks + tree walk)
64: - Constructor name != class name (superclass call) → MCSCC
65: - Superclass constructor call: not declared superclass → MCCBS; after object use → MCCBU; more than once → MCCMC; not assigned to first output → MCSCF/MCSCO; conditionalized → MCSCT; multiple outputs → MCSMO; superclass method name mismatch → MCSCM
66: 
67: ### F. Method signature rules
68: - Method has too many inputs/outputs → MCMIO (needs threshold; MATLAB limit ~ ?)
69: - TestParameterDefinition method not Static → MCMTP
70: - Property initialized to instance of the class itself → MCPIN
71: 
72: ## MUST fire
73: ```matlab
74: classdef Foo < Bar
75:     properties
76:         x double = 5
77:     end
78:     methods
79:         function y = f(self)
80:             y = self.x;
81:         end
82:     end
83: end
84: ```
85: (add specific invalid-attribute cases per check)
86: 
87: ## MUST NOT fire
88: ```matlab
89: classdef Foo
90:     properties
91:         x double = 5
92:     end
93:     methods
94:         function y = f(self)
95:             y = self.x;
96:         end
97:     end
98: end
99: ```
100: 
101: ## Files
102: - `crates/mlt_rules/src/language_spec.rs` — extend `check_class_rules`, add sub-check methods, module doc rows, tests.
103: - `docs/<id>.md` per check (26 pages).
104: - `docs/rules.md` — 26 rows.
105: - `zensical.toml` — 26 nav entries.
106: 
107: ## Tests
108: fires/not-fires per check; config disabled.
109: 
110: ## Pitfalls
111: - `ClassMeta` gives the parsed attributes/members — use it rather than raw tree walking where possible. For superclass-constructor call checks, a tree walk of the constructor method body is needed.
112: - Attribute `negated` field (AttributeMeta) — `~Hidden` etc.
113: - Confirm with astprobe which attribute names/values the parser extracts (e.g., does `properties (Access = private)` populate attributes?). See the existing MCSGA/MCSGP implementations for the established pattern.
114: - Many of these require a classdef with specific invalid constructs — build careful test fixtures.
115: 
116: ## REVIEW CORRECTIONS (MANDATORY)
117: 1. **DOCS**: sub-checks of LANGUAGE_SPEC_ENGINE. Update language_spec.rs module `//!` doc table with 26 rows. Do NOT create 26 individual pages unless Wave A/B convention requires per-check rows in docs/rules.md — prefer per-check rows for consistency, but reference a single docs/language-spec.md engine page for content.
118: 2. **MCMIO threshold = 64** inputs and 64 outputs (excluding `~`).
119: 3. **MCPSG**: interpretation = setter/getter declared abstract (function_signature, no body). Use FunctionMeta.is_abstract.
120: 4. **MCPIN**: property default_value contains a function_call to the class name itself (e.g. x Foo = Foo()). Check default_value text via tree walk or PropertyMeta.default_value.
121: 5. **Group E (constructor/superclass)**: FunctionMeta does NOT store the tree node. Use ctx.tree to find the function_definition whose name matches class.name (or match by byte_range). Walk its block for function_call nodes named "super" or matching a superclass name. Apply MCCBS/MCCBU/MCCMC/MCSCF/MCSCO/MCSCT/MCSMO/MCSCC/MCSCM.
122: 6. **MCCSOP/MCSCN**: walk method bodies for assignment nodes where LHS is obj.PropName (field_expression) and PropName is in a Constant properties block. MCCSOP=constructor only, MCSCN=any method.
123: 7. **Group A-D pure metadata**: use ClassMeta.is_sealed()/is_abstract()/has_attribute()/attribute_value(), AttributeMeta.negated. Check attributes on class + properties_blocks[i].attributes + methods_blocks[i].attributes.
124: 8. **Attribute negation**: use !a.negated when checking presence.
125: 9. Each of the 26 checks needs explicit MUST-fire + MUST-NOT-fire classdef fixtures (with all `end` keywords).
126: 10. All classdef test fixtures need proper `end` keywords.

(End of file - total 126 lines)
</content>

1: //! # Language Specification Errors Engine
2: //!
3: //! This module implements language specification error checks from MATLAB's Code Analyzer.
4: //! All checks are handled by a single file-level engine (`LanguageSpecEngine`) that performs
5: //! a full DFS traversal maintaining context stacks for parfor/spmd detection.
6: //!
7: //! ## Check IDs
8: //!
9: //! ### Parfor restrictions (PF* checks)
10: //!
11: //! | Check ID | Description                                      |
12: //! |----------|--------------------------------------------------|
13: //! | PFPF     | Nested parfor inside parfor                      |
14: //! | PFSPMD   | SPMD inside parfor                               |
15: //! | PFBRK    | break inside parfor                              |
16: //! | PFRTN    | return inside parfor                             |
17: //! | PFGLOB   | global declaration inside parfor                 |
18: //! | PFPERS   | persistent declaration inside parfor             |
19: //! | PFFORA   | Assignment to for-loop variable inside parfor    |
20: //! | PFXST    | Assignment to parfor loop variable               |
21: //! | PFNF     | Nested function call inside parfor               |
22: //!
23: //! ### SPMD restrictions (SP* checks)
24: //!
25: //! | Check ID | Description                                      |
26: //! |----------|--------------------------------------------------|
27: //! | SPNST    | parfor or spmd inside spmd                       |
28: //! | SPRET    | return/break/continue inside spmd                |
29: //! | SPGP     | global/persistent inside spmd                    |
30: //!
31: //! ### Class/OOP rules (MC* checks)
32: //!
33: //! | Check ID | Description                                      |
34: //! |----------|--------------------------------------------------|
35: //! | MCFIL    | Class name and file name don't match             |
36: //! | MCDIR    | Class name and @directory name don't match       |
37: //! | MCRED    | Property/event/enum name same as class name      |
38: //! | MCCBD    | Constructor not in class definition file         |
39: //! | MCS2I    | Setter must have exactly 2 inputs                |
40: //! | MCS1O    | Setter must have at most 1 output                |
41: //! | MCG1I    | Getter must have exactly 1 input                 |
42: //! | MCG1O    | Getter must have exactly 1 output                |
43: //! | MCEB     | Events defined in non-handle class               |
44: //! | MCANI    | Abstract property initialized                    |
45: //! | MCASC    | Abstract property in Sealed class                |
46: //! | MCSGA    | Set/get method in methods block with attributes  |
47: //! | MCSGP    | Set/get method refers to invalid property        |
48: //!
49: //! ### Function validation (FV* checks)
50: //!
51: //! | Check ID | Description                                      |
52: //! |----------|--------------------------------------------------|
53: //! | FVNST    | Arguments blocks in nested functions             |
54: //! | VTPOD    | Validation out of order (size, then class, then functions) |
55: //!
56: //! ### Other language spec checks
57: //!
58: //! | Check ID | Description                                      |
59: //! |----------|--------------------------------------------------|
60: //! | FCONV    | Variable name same as script name                |
61: //! | FCONF    | Local function name same as file name            |
62: //! | GPFST    | Global/persistent must precede first use         |
63: //! | GPNES    | Global/persistent must be in outermost function  |
64: //! | NPERS    | Persistent in script                             |
65: //! | ROWLN    | Matrix rows must be same length                  |
66: //! | FCNANS   | Function named 'ans'                             |
67: //! | CLANS    | Class named 'ans'                                |
68: //! | BRKFOR   | break outside loop                               |
69: //! | CONTFOR  | continue outside loop                            |
70: //! | IDXCOLND | END operator outside index expression            |
71: //!
72: //! ## Configuration
73: //!
74: //! ```toml
75: //! [lint.rules.LANGUAGE_SPEC_ENGINE]
76: //! severity = "error"
77: //! ```

79: use mlt_core::{Category, Config, Diagnostic, FileContext, Rule, Severity};
80: use serde::Deserialize;
81: 
82: use crate::analysis::metadata::{ClassMeta, FileMeta, FileType};
83: use crate::analysis::symbols::{DefKind, SymbolTable};

86: // Rule-specific configuration
87: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
88: 
89: /// Configuration for the language specification engine.
90: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Default)]
91: pub struct LanguageSpecConfig {
92:     // Reserved for future rule-specific parameters.
93: }
94: 
95: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
96: // Context tracking for DFS
97: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
98: 
99: /// Tracks what kind of loop/parallel context we are in.
100: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
101: enum LoopContext {
102:     /// Normal code (not inside any special parallel context).
103:     Normal,
104:     /// Inside a regular for/while loop.
105:     Loop,
106:     /// Inside a parfor loop.
107:     Parfor,
108:     /// Inside an spmd block.
109:     Spmd,
110: }
111: 
112: /// A frame on the context stack during DFS traversal.
113: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
114: struct ContextFrame {
115:     /// The type of context this frame represents.
116:     context: LoopContext,
117:     /// The parfor loop variable name (only set for Parfor context).
118:     parfor_var: Option<String>,
119:     /// The for-loop iterator variable names active in this parfor (accumulated).
120:     for_vars_in_parfor: Vec<String>,
121: }
122: 
123: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
124: // Rule implementation
125: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
126: 
127: /// Language specification error engine.
128: ///
129: /// Implements all language specification constraint checks as a single file-level
130: /// rule. Uses DFS traversal with a context stack to detect parfor/spmd/loop
131: /// violations, plus class metadata analysis for OOP rule checking.
132: pub struct LanguageSpecEngine {
133:     #[allow(dead_code)]
134:     config: LanguageSpecConfig,
135: }
136: 
137: impl LanguageSpecEngine {
138:     /// Factory constructor. Reads rule-specific params from config.
139:     pub fn from_config(config: &Config) -> Box<dyn Rule> {
140:         let rule_config: LanguageSpecConfig = config.rule_params("LANGUAGE_SPEC_ENGINE");
141:         Box::new(Self {
142:             config: rule_config,
143:         })
144:     }
145: }
146: 
147: impl Rule for LanguageSpecEngine {
148:     fn id(&self) -> &'static str {
149:         "LANGUAGE_SPEC_ENGINE"
150:     }
151: 
152:     fn description(&self) -> &'static str {
153:         "Language specification constraint violation"
154:     }
155: 
156:     fn severity(&self) -> Severity {
157:         Severity::Error
158:     }
159: 
160:     fn category(&self) -> Category {
161:         Category::LanguageSpecification
162:     }
163: 
164:     fn target_node_types(&self) -> &'static [&'static str] {
165:         &[] // File-level only
166:     }
167: 
168:     fn has_file_check(&self) -> bool {
169:         true
170:     }
171: 
172:     fn check_file(&self, ctx: &FileContext) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
173:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
174: 
175:         // Build metadata and symbol table
176:         let meta = FileMeta::build(ctx.tree, ctx.source);
177:         let symbol_table = SymbolTable::build(ctx.tree, ctx.source);
178: 
179:         // 1. DFS traversal for parfor/spmd/loop context violations
180:         let root = ctx.tree.root_node();
181:         let mut context_stack = vec![ContextFrame {
182:             context: LoopContext::Normal,
183:             parfor_var: None,
184:             for_vars_in_parfor: Vec::new(),
185:         }];
186:         self.check_dfs(root, ctx.source, &mut context_stack, &mut diagnostics);
187: 
188:         // 2. Class/OOP checks
189:         if let Some(ref class) = meta.class {
190:             self.check_class_rules(class, &meta, ctx, &mut diagnostics);
191:         }
192: 
193:         // 3. Function validation checks
194:         self.check_function_validation(&meta, ctx, &mut diagnostics);
195: 
196:         // 4. Script-level checks
197:         self.check_script_rules(&meta, &symbol_table, ctx, &mut diagnostics);
198: 
199:         // 5. Global/persistent ordering checks
200:         self.check_global_persistent_rules(&symbol_table, ctx, &mut diagnostics);
201: 
202:         // 6. break/continue outside loop (top-level check)
203:         self.check_break_continue_outside_loop(root, ctx.source, &mut diagnostics);
204: 
205:         // 7. Matrix row length checks
206:         self.check_matrix_rows(root, ctx.source, &mut diagnostics);
207: 
208:         // 8. Function/class named 'ans'
209:         self.check_ans_naming(&meta, ctx, &mut diagnostics);
210: 
211:         // 9. END operator outside index expression
212:         self.check_end_operator(root, ctx.source, &mut diagnostics);
213: 
214:         // 10. Local function name same as file name

217:         diagnostics
218:     }
219: }

221: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
222: // DFS traversal for parfor/spmd/loop context checks
223: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
224: 
225: impl LanguageSpecEngine {
226:     /// DFS traversal to detect parfor/spmd context violations.
227:     fn check_dfs(
228:         &self,
229:         node: tree_sitter::Node,
230:         source: &str,
231:         context_stack: &mut Vec<ContextFrame>,
232:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
233:     ) {
234:         let kind = node.kind();
235:         let current_context = context_stack.last().map(|f| f.context).unwrap_or(LoopContext::Normal);
236: 
237:         match kind {
238:             "for_statement" => {
239:                 let is_parfor = self.is_parfor_node(node);
240: 
241:                 if is_parfor {
242:                     // This is a parfor loop
243: 
244:                     // Check: PFPF — nested parfor inside parfor
245:                     if current_context == LoopContext::Parfor {
246:                         let pos = node.start_position();
247:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
248:                             rule_id: "PFPF",
249:                             message: "Nested parfor is not allowed inside a parfor loop"
250:                                 .to_string(),
251:                             severity: Severity::Error,
252:                             byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
253:                             line: pos.row + 1,
254:                             column: pos.column + 1,
255:                             fix: None,
256:                         });
257:                     }
258: 
259:                     // Check: SPNST — parfor inside spmd
260:                     if current_context == LoopContext::Spmd {
261:                         let pos = node.start_position();
262:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
263:                             rule_id: "SPNST",
264:                             message: "parfor is not allowed inside an spmd block".to_string(),
265:                             severity: Severity::Error,
266:                             byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
267:                             line: pos.row + 1,
268:                             column: pos.column + 1,
269:                             fix: None,
270:                         });
271:                     }
272: 
273:                     // Extract the parfor loop variable
274:                     let parfor_var = self.extract_for_variable(node, source);
275: 
276:                     // Push parfor context and recurse
277:                     context_stack.push(ContextFrame {
278:                         context: LoopContext::Parfor,
279:                         parfor_var,
280:                         for_vars_in_parfor: Vec::new(),
281:                     });
282:                     self.visit_children(node, source, context_stack, diagnostics);
283:                     context_stack.pop();
284:                 } else {
285:                     // Normal for loop
286:                     if current_context == LoopContext::Parfor {
287:                         // Track the for-loop variable inside parfor
288:                         if let Some(var) = self.extract_for_variable(node, source) {
289:                             if let Some(frame) = context_stack.last_mut() {
290:                                 frame.for_vars_in_parfor.push(var);
291:                             }
292:                         }
293:                         // Stay in Parfor context
294:                         self.visit_children(node, source, context_stack, diagnostics);
295:                         // Remove the for variable from tracking
296:                         if let Some(frame) = context_stack.last_mut() {
297:                             frame.for_vars_in_parfor.pop();
298:                         }
299:                     } else {
300:                         // Push normal loop context
301:                         context_stack.push(ContextFrame {
302:                             context: LoopContext::Loop,
303:                             parfor_var: None,
304:                             for_vars_in_parfor: Vec::new(),
305:                         });
306:                         self.visit_children(node, source, context_stack, diagnostics);
307:                         context_stack.pop();
308:                     }
309:                 }
310:                 return;
311:             }
312: 
313:             "while_statement" => {
314:                 if current_context == LoopContext::Parfor {
315:                     // Stay in Parfor context for while inside parfor
316:                     self.visit_children(node, source, context_stack, diagnostics);
317:                 } else {
318:                     // Push normal loop context
319:                     context_stack.push(ContextFrame {
320:                         context: LoopContext::Loop,
321:                         parfor_var: None,
322:                         for_vars_in_parfor: Vec::new(),
323:                     });
324:                     self.visit_children(node, source, context_stack, diagnostics);
325:                     context_stack.pop();
326:                 }
327:                 return;
328:             }
329: 
330:             "spmd_statement" => {
331:                 // Check: PFSPMD — spmd inside parfor
332:                 if current_context == LoopContext::Parfor {
333:                     let pos = node.start_position();
334:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
335:                         rule_id: "PFSPMD",
336:                         message: "spmd is not allowed inside a parfor loop".to_string(),
337:                         severity: Severity::Error,
338:                         byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
339:                         line: pos.row + 1,
340:                         column: pos.column + 1,
341:                         fix: None,
342:                     });
343:                 }
344: 
345:                 // Check: SPNST — spmd inside spmd
346:                 if current_context == LoopContext::Spmd {
347:                     let pos = node.start_position();
348:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
349:                         rule_id: "SPNST",
350:                         message: "spmd is not allowed inside another spmd block".to_string(),
351:                         severity: Severity::Error,
352:                         byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
353:                         line: pos.row + 1,
354:                         column: pos.column + 1,
355:                         fix: None,
356:                     });
357:                 }
358: 
359:                 // Push spmd context and recurse
360:                 context_stack.push(ContextFrame {
361:                     context: LoopContext::Spmd,
362:                     parfor_var: None,
363:                     for_vars_in_parfor: Vec::new(),
364:                 });
365:                 self.visit_children(node, source, context_stack, diagnostics);
366:                 context_stack.pop();
367:                 return;
368:             }
369: 
370:             "break_statement" => {
371:                 // Check: PFBRK — break inside parfor
372:                 if current_context == LoopContext::Parfor {
373:                     let pos = node.start_position();
374:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
375:                         rule_id: "PFBRK",
376:                         message: "break is not allowed inside a parfor loop".to_string(),
377:                         severity: Severity::Error,
378:                         byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
379:                         line: pos.row + 1,
380:                         column: pos.column + 1,
381:                         fix: None,
382:                     });
383:                 }
384:                 // Check: SPRET — break inside spmd
385:                 if current_context == LoopContext::Spmd {
386:                     let pos = node.start_position();
387:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
388:                         rule_id: "SPRET",
389:                         message: "break is not allowed inside an spmd block".to_string(),
390:                         severity: Severity::Error,
391:                         byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
392:                         line: pos.row + 1,
393:                         column: pos.column + 1,
394:                         fix: None,
395:                     });
396:                 }
397:             }
398: 
399:             "continue_statement" if current_context == LoopContext::Spmd => {
400:                 // Check: SPRET — continue inside spmd
401:                 let pos = node.start_position();
402:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
403:                     rule_id: "SPRET",
404:                     message: "continue is not allowed inside an spmd block".to_string(),
405:                     severity: Severity::Error,
406:                     byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
407:                     line: pos.row + 1,
408:                     column: pos.column + 1,
409:                     fix: None,
410:                 });
411:             }
412: 
413:             "return_statement" => {
414:                 // Check: PFRTN — return inside parfor
415:                 if current_context == LoopContext::Parfor {
416:                     let pos = node.start_position();
417:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
418:                         rule_id: "PFRTN",
419:                         message: "return is not allowed inside a parfor loop".to_string(),
420:                         severity: Severity::Error,
421:                         byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
422:                         line: pos.row + 1,
423:                         column: pos.column + 1,
424:                         fix: None,
425:                     });
426:                 }
427:                 // Check: SPRET — return inside spmd
428:                 if current_context == LoopContext::Spmd {
429:                     let pos = node.start_position();
430:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
431:                         rule_id: "SPRET",
432:                         message: "return is not allowed inside an spmd block".to_string(),
433:                         severity: Severity::Error,
434:                         byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
435:                         line: pos.row + 1,
436:                         column: pos.column + 1,
437:                         fix: None,
438:                     });
439:                 }
440:             }
441: 
442:             "global_operator" => {
443:                 // Check: PFGLOB — global inside parfor
444:                 if current_context == LoopContext::Parfor {
445:                     let pos = node.start_position();
446:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
447:                         rule_id: "PFGLOB",
448:                         message: "global declarations are not allowed inside a parfor loop"
449:                             .to_string(),
450:                         severity: Severity::Error,
451:                         byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
452:                         line: pos.row + 1,
453:                         column: pos.column + 1,
454:                         fix: None,
455:                     });
456:                 }
457:                 // Check: SPGP — global inside spmd
458:                 if current_context == LoopContext::Spmd {
459:                     let pos = node.start_position();
460:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
461:                         rule_id: "SPGP",
462:                         message: "global declarations are not allowed inside an spmd block"
463:                             .to_string(),
464:                         severity: Severity::Error,
465:                         byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
466:                         line: pos.row + 1,
467:                         column: pos.column + 1,
468:                         fix: None,
469:                     });
470:                 }
471:             }
472: 
473:             "persistent_operator" => {
474:                 // Check: PFPERS — persistent inside parfor
475:                 if current_context == LoopContext::Parfor {
476:                     let pos = node.start_position();
477:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
478:                         rule_id: "PFPERS",
479:                         message: "persistent declarations are not allowed inside a parfor loop"
480:                             .to_string(),
481:                         severity: Severity::Error,
482:                         byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
483:                         line: pos.row + 1,
484:                         column: pos.column + 1,
485:                         fix: None,
486:                     });
487:                 }
488:                 // Check: SPGP — persistent inside spmd
489:                 if current_context == LoopContext::Spmd {
490:                     let pos = node.start_position();
491:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
492:                         rule_id: "SPGP",
493:                         message: "persistent declarations are not allowed inside an spmd block"
494:                             .to_string(),
495:                         severity: Severity::Error,
496:                         byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
497:                         line: pos.row + 1,
498:                         column: pos.column + 1,
499:                         fix: None,
500:                     });
501:                 }
502:             }
503: 
504:             "assignment" if current_context == LoopContext::Parfor => {
505:                 // Check: PFXST — assignment to parfor loop variable
506:                 // Check: PFFORA — assignment to for-loop variable inside parfor
507:                 if let Some(lhs_name) = self.extract_assignment_lhs_name(node, source) {
508:                     // PFXST: assignment to the parfor loop variable itself
509:                     let parfor_var = context_stack
510:                         .iter()
511:                         .rev()
512:                         .find(|f| f.context == LoopContext::Parfor)
513:                         .and_then(|f| f.parfor_var.as_deref());
514:                     if let Some(pv) = parfor_var {
515:                         if lhs_name == pv {
516:                             let pos = node.start_position();
517:                             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
518:                                 rule_id: "PFXST",
519:                                 message: format!(
520:                                     "Assignment to parfor loop variable '{lhs_name}' is not allowed"
521:                                 ),
522:                                 severity: Severity::Error,
523:                                 byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
524:                                 line: pos.row + 1,
525:                                 column: pos.column + 1,
526:                                 fix: None,
527:                             });
528:                         }
529:                     }
530: 
531:                     // PFFORA: assignment to a for-loop variable inside the parfor
532:                     let for_vars: Vec<String> = context_stack
533:                         .iter()
534:                         .rev()
535:                         .find(|f| f.context == LoopContext::Parfor)
536:                         .map(|f| f.for_vars_in_parfor.clone())
537:                         .unwrap_or_default();
538:                     if for_vars.contains(&lhs_name) {
539:                         let pos = node.start_position();
540:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
541:                             rule_id: "PFFORA",
542:                             message: format!(
543:                                 "Assignment to for-loop variable '{lhs_name}' inside parfor is not allowed"
544:                             ),
545:                             severity: Severity::Error,
546:                             byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
547:                             line: pos.row + 1,
548:                             column: pos.column + 1,
549:                             fix: None,
550:                         });
551:                     }
552:                 }
553:             }
554: 
555:             "function_definition" => {
556:                 // Check: PFNF — nested function definition inside parfor
557:                 if current_context == LoopContext::Parfor {
558:                     let pos = node.start_position();
559:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
560:                         rule_id: "PFNF",
561:                         message: "Nested function definitions are not allowed inside a parfor loop"
562:                             .to_string(),
563:                         severity: Severity::Error,
564:                         byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
565:                         line: pos.row + 1,
566:                         column: pos.column + 1,
567:                         fix: None,
568:                     });
569:                     // Don't recurse into nested function_definitions from parfor context
570:                     return;
571:                 }
572:                 if current_context == LoopContext::Spmd {
573:                     // Don't recurse into function_definitions from spmd context
574:                     return;
575:                 }
576:                 // For Normal/Loop context, recurse normally into function body
577:                 // (but reset context to Normal since function creates its own scope)
578:                 context_stack.push(ContextFrame {
579:                     context: LoopContext::Normal,
580:                     parfor_var: None,
581:                     for_vars_in_parfor: Vec::new(),
582:                 });
583:                 self.visit_children(node, source, context_stack, diagnostics);
584:                 context_stack.pop();
585:                 return;
586:             }
587: 
588:             _ => {}
589:         }
590: 
591:         // Recurse into children
592:         self.visit_children(node, source, context_stack, diagnostics);
593:     }
594: 
595:     /// Visit all children of a node during DFS traversal.
596:     fn visit_children(
597:         &self,
598:         node: tree_sitter::Node,
599:         source: &str,
600:         context_stack: &mut Vec<ContextFrame>,
601:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
602:     ) {
603:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
604:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
605:             self.check_dfs(child, source, context_stack, diagnostics);
606:         }
607:     }
608: 
609:     /// Check if a `for_statement` node is actually a `parfor` loop.
610:     ///
611:     /// In tree-sitter-matlab, `parfor i = 1:10 ... end` is parsed as a
612:     /// `for_statement` with a child node of kind `"parfor"` (instead of `"for"`).
613:     fn is_parfor_node(&self, node: tree_sitter::Node) -> bool {
614:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
615:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
616:             if child.kind() == "parfor" {
617:                 return true;
618:             }
619:             // Stop early once we hit the iterator (keyword comes before it)
620:             if child.kind() == "iterator" {
621:                 break;
622:             }
623:         }
624:         false
625:     }
626: 
627:     /// Extract the loop variable from a `for_statement` (works for both for and parfor).
628:     fn extract_for_variable(&self, node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str) -> Option<String> {
629:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
630:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
631:             if child.kind() == "iterator" {
632:                 return self.extract_iterator_variable(child, source);
633:             }
634:         }
635:         None
636:     }
637: 
638:     /// Extract the variable name from an iterator node.
639:     fn extract_iterator_variable(
640:         &self,
641:         iter_node: tree_sitter::Node,
642:         source: &str,
643:     ) -> Option<String> {
644:         let mut cursor = iter_node.walk();
645:         for child in iter_node.children(&mut cursor) {
646:             if child.kind() == "identifier" {
647:                 return Some(node_text(child, source).to_string());
648:             }
649:         }
650:         None
651:     }
652: 
653:     /// Extract the LHS variable name from a simple assignment.
654:     fn extract_assignment_lhs_name(
655:         &self,
656:         node: tree_sitter::Node,
657:         source: &str,
658:     ) -> Option<String> {
659:         let lhs = node.child_by_field_name("left")?;
660:         if lhs.kind() == "identifier" {
661:             Some(node_text(lhs, source).to_string())
662:         } else {
663:             None
664:         }
665:     }
666: }

672: impl LanguageSpecEngine {
673:     /// Check all class/OOP related rules.
674:     fn check_class_rules(
675:         &self,
676:         class: &ClassMeta,
677:         meta: &FileMeta,
678:         ctx: &FileContext,
679:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
680:     ) {
681:         self.check_mcfil(class, ctx, diagnostics);
682:         self.check_mcdir(class, ctx, diagnostics);
683:         self.check_mcred(class, diagnostics);
684:         self.check_mccbd(class, meta, ctx, diagnostics);
685:         self.check_setter_getter_signatures(class, meta, diagnostics);
686:         self.check_mceb(class, diagnostics);
687:         self.check_mcani(class, diagnostics);
688:         self.check_mcasc(class, diagnostics);
689:         self.check_mcsga(class, meta, diagnostics);
690:         self.check_mcsgp(class, meta, diagnostics);

693:     /// MCFIL: Class name must match file name.
694:     fn check_mcfil(
695:         &self,
696:         class: &ClassMeta,
697:         ctx: &FileContext,
698:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
699:     ) {
700:         let file_stem = ctx
701:             .file_path
702:             .file_stem()
703:             .and_then(|s| s.to_str())
704:             .unwrap_or("");
705:         if !file_stem.is_empty() && file_stem != class.name {
706:             // Don't fire if the file is in a @directory (MCDIR handles that)
707:             let in_at_dir = ctx
708:                 .file_path
709:                 .parent()
710:                 .and_then(|p| p.file_name())
711:                 .and_then(|n| n.to_str())
712:                 .is_some_and(|dir| dir.starts_with('@'));
713:             if !in_at_dir {
714:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
715:                     rule_id: "MCFIL",
716:                     message: format!(
717:                         "Class name '{}' does not match file name '{}'",
718:                         class.name, file_stem
719:                     ),
720:                     severity: Severity::Error,
721:                     byte_range: class.byte_range.clone(),
722:                     line: class.line,
723:                     column: 1,
724:                     fix: None,
725:                 });
726:             }
727:         }
728:     }
729: 
730:     /// MCDIR: Class name must match @directory name.
731:     fn check_mcdir(
732:         &self,
733:         class: &ClassMeta,
734:         ctx: &FileContext,
735:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
736:     ) {
737:         if let Some(parent_dir) = ctx.file_path.parent() {
738:             if let Some(dir_name) = parent_dir.file_name().and_then(|n| n.to_str()) {
739:                 if let Some(stripped) = dir_name.strip_prefix('@') {
740:                     if stripped != class.name {
741:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
742:                             rule_id: "MCDIR",
743:                             message: format!(
744:                                 "Class name '{}' does not match @directory name '@{}'",
745:                                 class.name, stripped
746:                             ),
747:                             severity: Severity::Error,
748:                             byte_range: class.byte_range.clone(),
749:                             line: class.line,
750:                             column: 1,
751:                             fix: None,
752:                         });
753:                     }
754:                 }
755:             }
756:         }
757:     }
758: 
759:     /// MCRED: Property/event/enum name same as class name.
760:     fn check_mcred(&self, class: &ClassMeta, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
761:         // Check properties
762:         for pb in &class.properties_blocks {
763:             for prop in &pb.properties {
764:                 if prop.name == class.name {
765:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
766:                         rule_id: "MCRED",
767:                         message: format!(
768:                             "Property '{}' has the same name as the class",
769:                             prop.name
770:                         ),
771:                         severity: Severity::Error,
772:                         byte_range: prop.byte_range.clone(),
773:                         line: prop.line,
774:                         column: 1,
775:                         fix: None,
776:                     });
777:                 }
778:             }
779:         }
780: 
781:         // Check events
782:         for eb in &class.events_blocks {
783:             for event in &eb.events {
784:                 if *event == class.name {
785:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
786:                         rule_id: "MCRED",
787:                         message: format!(
788:                             "Event '{}' has the same name as the class",
789:                             event
790:                         ),
791:                         severity: Severity::Error,
792:                         byte_range: class.byte_range.clone(),
793:                         line: class.line,
794:                         column: 1,
795:                         fix: None,
796:                     });
797:                 }
798:             }
799:         }
800: 
801:         // Check enumeration members
802:         for enb in &class.enumeration_blocks {
803:             for member in &enb.members {
804:                 if *member == class.name {
805:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
806:                         rule_id: "MCRED",
807:                         message: format!(
808:                             "Enumeration member '{}' has the same name as the class",
809:                             member
810:                         ),
811:                         severity: Severity::Error,
812:                         byte_range: class.byte_range.clone(),
813:                         line: class.line,
814:                         column: 1,
815:                         fix: None,
816:                     });
817:                 }
818:             }
819:         }
820:     }

822:     /// MCCBD: Constructor must be defined in the class definition file.
823:     fn check_mccbd(
824:         &self,
825:         class: &ClassMeta,
826:         meta: &FileMeta,
827:         ctx: &FileContext,
828:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
829:     ) {
830:         // If we're in a @directory class, the constructor may be in a separate file.
831:         // Check if there's a constructor in the methods blocks.
832:         let in_at_dir = ctx
833:             .file_path
834:             .parent()
835:             .and_then(|p| p.file_name())
836:             .and_then(|n| n.to_str())
837:             .is_some_and(|dir| dir.starts_with('@'));
838: 
839:         if in_at_dir {
840:             // In @directory mode, skip this check — constructors can be in separate files.
841:             return;
842:         }
843: 
844:         // For single-file classes, check that a constructor is defined for non-abstract classes.
845:         // Actually, MCCBD checks that if a constructor IS defined, it should be in the class file.
846:         // This is mainly relevant for @folder classes where methods can be in separate files.
847:         // For single-file classes we verify the constructor is in a methods block (not local func).
848:         for func in &meta.local_functions {
849:             if func.name == class.name {
850:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
851:                     rule_id: "MCCBD",
852:                     message: format!(
853:                         "Constructor '{}' should be defined inside a methods block, not as a local function",
854:                         class.name
855:                     ),
856:                     severity: Severity::Error,
857:                     byte_range: func.byte_range.clone(),
858:                     line: func.line,
859:                     column: 1,
860:                     fix: None,
861:                 });
862:             }
863:         }
864:     }

866:     /// MCS2I, MCS1O, MCG1I, MCG1O: Setter/getter signature validation.
867:     fn check_setter_getter_signatures(
868:         &self,
869:         _class: &ClassMeta,
870:         meta: &FileMeta,
871:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
872:     ) {
873:         for func in &meta.functions {
874:             if func.is_setter {
875:                 // MCS2I: Setter must have exactly 2 inputs (obj, value)
876:                 if func.inputs.len() != 2 {
877:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
878:                         rule_id: "MCS2I",
879:                         message: format!(
880:                             "Setter '{}' must have exactly 2 input arguments (obj, value), found {}",
881:                             func.name,
882:                             func.inputs.len()
883:                         ),
884:                         severity: Severity::Error,
885:                         byte_range: func.byte_range.clone(),
886:                         line: func.line,
887:                         column: 1,
888:                         fix: None,
889:                     });
890:                 }
891: 
892:                 // MCS1O: Setter must have at most 1 output (obj)
893:                 if func.outputs.len() > 1 {
894:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
895:                         rule_id: "MCS1O",
896:                         message: format!(
897:                             "Setter '{}' must have at most 1 output argument, found {}",
898:                             func.name,
899:                             func.outputs.len()
900:                         ),
901:                         severity: Severity::Error,
902:                         byte_range: func.byte_range.clone(),
903:                         line: func.line,
904:                         column: 1,
905:                         fix: None,
906:                     });
907:                 }
908:             }
909: 
910:             if func.is_getter {
911:                 // MCG1I: Getter must have exactly 1 input (obj)
912:                 if func.inputs.len() != 1 {
913:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
914:                         rule_id: "MCG1I",
915:                         message: format!(
916:                             "Getter '{}' must have exactly 1 input argument (obj), found {}",
917:                             func.name,
918:                             func.inputs.len()
919:                         ),
920:                         severity: Severity::Error,
921:                         byte_range: func.byte_range.clone(),
922:                         line: func.line,
923:                         column: 1,
924:                         fix: None,
925:                     });
926:                 }
927: 
928:                 // MCG1O: Getter must have exactly 1 output
929:                 if func.outputs.len() != 1 {
930:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
931:                         rule_id: "MCG1O",
932:                         message: format!(
933:                             "Getter '{}' must have exactly 1 output argument, found {}",
934:                             func.name,
935:                             func.outputs.len()
936:                         ),
937:                         severity: Severity::Error,
938:                         byte_range: func.byte_range.clone(),
939:                         line: func.line,
940:                         column: 1,
941:                         fix: None,
942:                     });
943:                 }
944:             }
945:         }
946:     }

948:     /// MCEB: Events can only be defined in handle classes.
949:     fn check_mceb(&self, class: &ClassMeta, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
950:         if !class.events_blocks.is_empty() && !class.is_handle() {
951:             for eb in &class.events_blocks {
952:                 if !eb.events.is_empty() {

956:                             .to_string(),
957:                         severity: Severity::Error,
958:                         byte_range: class.byte_range.clone(),
959:                         line: class.line,
960:                         column: 1,
961:                         fix: None,
962:                     });
963:                     break; // Only report once per class
964:                 }
965:             }
966:         }
967:     }

969:     /// MCANI: Abstract property must not have a default value.
970:     fn check_mcani(&self, class: &ClassMeta, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {

980:                                 prop.name

983:                             byte_range: prop.byte_range.clone(),
984:                             line: prop.line,
985:                             column: 1,
986:                             fix: None,
987:                         });
988:                     }
989:                 }
990:             }
991:         }
992:     }

994:     /// MCASC: Abstract properties cannot be defined in Sealed classes.
995:     fn check_mcasc(&self, class: &ClassMeta, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
996:         if class.is_sealed() {
997:             for pb in &class.properties_blocks {
998:                 let is_abstract = pb.attributes.iter().any(|a| a.name == "Abstract" && !a.negated);

1003:                             message: format!(
1004:                                 "Abstract property '{}' cannot be defined in a Sealed class",
1005:                                 prop.name
1006:                             ),
1007:                             severity: Severity::Error,
1008:                             byte_range: prop.byte_range.clone(),
1009:                             line: prop.line,
1010:                             column: 1,
1011:                             fix: None,
1012:                         });
1013:                     }
1014:                 }
1015:             }
1016:         }

1019:     /// MCSGA: Set/get methods should not be in methods blocks with attributes.
1020:     fn check_mcsga(
1021:         &self,
1022:         _class: &ClassMeta,
1023:         meta: &FileMeta,
1024:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
1025:     ) {

1106:     /// FVNST: Arguments blocks in nested functions are not allowed.
1107:     fn check_fvnst(&self, ctx: &FileContext, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
1108:         // Walk the tree to find nested function_definitions with arguments blocks
1109:         let root = ctx.tree.root_node();
1110:         Self::find_nested_functions_with_args(root, 0, diagnostics);
1111:     }
1112: 
1113:     /// Recursively find nested functions that have arguments blocks.
1114:     fn find_nested_functions_with_args(
1115:         node: tree_sitter::Node,
1116:         depth: usize,
1117:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
1118:     ) {
1119:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
1120:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
1121:             if child.kind() == "function_definition" {
1122:                 if depth > 0 {
1123:                     // This is a nested function; check for arguments blocks
1124:                     let mut inner_cursor = child.walk();
1125:                     for inner in child.children(&mut inner_cursor) {
1126:                         if inner.kind() == "arguments_statement" {
1127:                             let pos = inner.start_position();
1128:                             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
1129:                                 rule_id: "FVNST",
1130:                                 message: "Arguments blocks are not allowed in nested functions"
1131:                                     .to_string(),
1132:                                 severity: Severity::Error,
1133:                                 byte_range: inner.start_byte()..inner.end_byte(),
1134:                                 line: pos.row + 1,
1135:                                 column: pos.column + 1,
1136:                                 fix: None,
1137:                             });
1138:                         }
1139:                     }
1140:                 }
1141:                 // Recurse into the function definition at depth+1
1142:                 Self::find_nested_functions_with_args(child, depth + 1, diagnostics);
1143:             } else if child.kind() != "methods" && child.kind() != "class_definition" {
1144:                 // Continue recursing but don't increase depth for non-function nodes
1145:                 // Skip methods blocks (class methods are not nested functions)
1146:                 Self::find_nested_functions_with_args(child, depth, diagnostics);

1148:         }
1149:     }

1157:     fn check_vtpod(&self, _meta: &FileMeta, _diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
1158:         // Currently a no-op stub. The tree-sitter grammar enforces the
1159:         // basic ordering. A future implementation will check for degenerate
1160:         // cases where user annotations conflict with MATLAB's expected order.
1161:     }
1162: }

1: //! # Function/Class Metadata Extraction
2: //!
3: //! Extracts structural metadata from a parsed MATLAB file, including:
4: //!
5: //! - **File type** detection (script, function file, class file)
6: //! - **Function metadata**: name, inputs, outputs, argument validation blocks,
7: //!   setter/getter/constructor detection, method attributes
8: //! - **Class metadata**: name, superclasses, attributes, properties blocks,
9: //!   methods blocks, events blocks, enumeration blocks
10: //! - **Property metadata**: name, dimensions, type constraints, validators,
11: //!   default values
12: //!
13: //! ## Usage
14: //!
15: //! ```ignore
16: //! use mlt_rules::analysis::metadata::FileMeta;
17: //!
18: //! let meta = FileMeta::build(tree, source);
19: //! match meta.file_type {
20: //!     FileType::ClassFile => {
21: //!         let class = meta.class.as_ref().unwrap();
22: //!         println!("Class: {}", class.name);
23: //!         for prop in meta.all_properties() {
24: //!             println!("  property: {}", prop.name);
25: //!         }
26: //!     }
27: //!     FileType::FunctionFile => {
28: //!         if let Some(main) = meta.main_function() {
29: //!             println!("Main function: {}", main.name);
30: //!         }
31: //!     }
32: //!     FileType::Script => println!("Script file"),
33: //! }
34: //! ```
35: 
36: use std::ops::Range;
37: use tree_sitter::{Node, Tree};
38: 
39: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
40: // Core types
41: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
42: 
43: /// The type of MATLAB file.
44: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
45: pub enum FileType {
46:     /// Script file (no `function_definition` at top level, or function after statements).
47:     Script,
48:     /// Function file (starts with `function_definition`).
49:     FunctionFile,
50:     /// Class definition file (contains `class_definition`).
51:     ClassFile,
52: }
53: 
54: /// Metadata about a function definition.
55: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
56: pub struct FunctionMeta {
57:     /// Function name.
58:     pub name: String,
59:     /// Input argument names.
60:     pub inputs: Vec<String>,
61:     /// Output argument names (includes `~` as placeholder).
62:     pub outputs: Vec<String>,
63:     /// Whether this is a constructor (name matches class name).
64:     pub is_constructor: bool,
65:     /// Whether this is a property setter (name starts with `set.`).
66:     pub is_setter: bool,
67:     /// Whether this is a property getter (name starts with `get.`).
68:     pub is_getter: bool,
69:     /// Whether this function has an `arguments` validation block.
70:     pub has_arguments_block: bool,
71:     /// The argument validation entries (if any).
72:     pub argument_validations: Vec<ArgValidation>,
73:     /// Byte range of the function node.
74:     pub byte_range: Range<usize>,
75:     /// 1-indexed start line.
76:     pub line: usize,
77:     /// 1-indexed end line.
78:     pub end_line: usize,
79:     /// Whether defined inside a methods block (is a method).
80:     pub is_method: bool,
81:     /// Whether this is an abstract method (`function_signature`, no body).
82:     pub is_abstract: bool,
83:     /// Attributes from the enclosing methods block (if any).
84:     pub method_attributes: Vec<AttributeMeta>,
85: }
86: 
87: /// An argument validation entry from an `arguments` block.
88: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
89: pub struct ArgValidation {
90:     /// Argument name.
91:     pub name: String,
92:     /// Size constraint (e.g., `"(1,3)"`), if specified.
93:     pub dimensions: Option<String>,
94:     /// Class/type constraint (e.g., `"double"`), if specified.
95:     pub type_constraint: Option<String>,
96:     /// Validation functions (e.g., `["mustBePositive"]`).
97:     pub validators: Vec<String>,
98:     /// Default value expression text, if specified.
99:     pub default_value: Option<String>,
100: }
101: 
102: /// An attribute on a class, properties block, methods block, or events block.
103: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
104: pub struct AttributeMeta {
105:     /// Attribute name (e.g., `"Access"`, `"Sealed"`, `"Abstract"`).
106:     pub name: String,
107:     /// Attribute value as source text (e.g., `"private"`, `"true"`), or `None` if bare/negated.
108:     pub value: Option<String>,
109:     /// Whether the attribute is negated (e.g., `~Hidden`).
110:     pub negated: bool,
111: }
112: 
113: /// Metadata about a class property.
114: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
115: pub struct PropertyMeta {
116:     /// Property name.
117:     pub name: String,
118:     /// Size constraint, if specified.
119:     pub dimensions: Option<String>,
120:     /// Type constraint, if specified.
121:     pub type_constraint: Option<String>,
122:     /// Validation functions.
123:     pub validators: Vec<String>,
124:     /// Default value expression text.
125:     pub default_value: Option<String>,
126:     /// Whether this property has a default value.
127:     pub has_default: bool,
128:     /// Byte range.
129:     pub byte_range: Range<usize>,
130:     /// 1-indexed line.
131:     pub line: usize,
132: }
133: 
134: /// Metadata about a `properties ... end` block.
135: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
136: pub struct PropertiesBlockMeta {
137:     /// Attributes on this properties block.
138:     pub attributes: Vec<AttributeMeta>,
139:     /// Properties defined in this block.
140:     pub properties: Vec<PropertyMeta>,
141: }
142: 
143: /// Metadata about a `methods ... end` block.
144: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
145: pub struct MethodsBlockMeta {
146:     /// Attributes on this methods block.
147:     pub attributes: Vec<AttributeMeta>,
148:     /// Functions (methods) defined in this block.
149:     pub methods: Vec<FunctionMeta>,
150: }
151: 
152: /// Metadata about an `events ... end` block.
153: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
154: pub struct EventsBlockMeta {
155:     /// Attributes on this events block.
156:     pub attributes: Vec<AttributeMeta>,
157:     /// Event names.
158:     pub events: Vec<String>,
159: }
160: 
161: /// Metadata about an `enumeration ... end` block.
162: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
163: pub struct EnumerationBlockMeta {
164:     /// Enumeration member names.
165:     pub members: Vec<String>,
166: }
167: 
168: /// Metadata about a class definition.
169: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
170: pub struct ClassMeta {
171:     /// Class name.
172:     pub name: String,
173:     /// Superclass names.
174:     pub superclasses: Vec<String>,
175:     /// Class-level attributes.
176:     pub attributes: Vec<AttributeMeta>,
177:     /// Properties blocks.
178:     pub properties_blocks: Vec<PropertiesBlockMeta>,
179:     /// Methods blocks.
180:     pub methods_blocks: Vec<MethodsBlockMeta>,
181:     /// Events blocks.
182:     pub events_blocks: Vec<EventsBlockMeta>,
183:     /// Enumeration blocks.
184:     pub enumeration_blocks: Vec<EnumerationBlockMeta>,
185:     /// Byte range of the `class_definition` node.
186:     pub byte_range: Range<usize>,
187:     /// 1-indexed start line.
188:     pub line: usize,
189: }
190: 
191: /// Complete file metadata extracted from a single parse tree.
192: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
193: pub struct FileMeta {
194:     /// The type of this file (script, function, or class).
195:     pub file_type: FileType,
196:     /// The class definition, if this is a class file.
197:     pub class: Option<ClassMeta>,
198:     /// All function definitions (including methods if class file).
199:     /// For function files: first is the main function, rest are local functions.
200:     pub functions: Vec<FunctionMeta>,
201:     /// Local functions defined after the class definition (in class files)
202:     /// or after the main function (in function files).
203:     pub local_functions: Vec<FunctionMeta>,
204: }
205: 
206: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
207: // Helpers
208: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
209: 
210: /// Extract the source text covered by a node.
211: fn node_text<'a>(node: Node, source: &'a str) -> &'a str {
212:     &source[node.start_byte()..node.end_byte()]
213: }
214: 
215: /// Extract attributes from an `attributes` node.
216: ///
217: /// Each `attribute` child represents a single attribute entry.
218: /// Attributes can be:
219: /// - Bare: `Sealed` (value is `None`, treated as `true`)
220: /// - Valued: `Access = private`
221: /// - Negated: `~Hidden` (negated flag set)
222: fn extract_attributes(attrs_node: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<AttributeMeta> {
223:     let mut attrs = Vec::new();
224:     let mut cursor = attrs_node.walk();
225: 
226:     for child in attrs_node.children(&mut cursor) {
227:         if child.kind() != "attribute" {
228:             continue;
229:         }
230: 
231:         let text = node_text(child, source).trim();
232:         let negated = text.starts_with('~');
233: 
234:         // Find the attribute name — first identifier child.
235:         let name = find_first_child_of_kind(child, "identifier")
236:             .map(|n| node_text(n, source).to_string())
237:             .unwrap_or_default();
238: 
239:         if name.is_empty() {
240:             continue;
241:         }
242: 
243:         // Look for `= value` portion.  The value is everything after the `=`.
244:         // In the grammar an attribute with a value has the identifier, then `=`, then
245:         // one or more value children (which may be identifiers, strings, etc.).
246:         let value = extract_attribute_value(child, source);
247: 
248:         attrs.push(AttributeMeta {
249:             name,
250:             value,
251:             negated,
252:         });
253:     }
254: 
255:     attrs
256: }
257: 
258: /// Extract the value portion of an `attribute` node (everything after `=`).
259: ///
260: /// Returns `None` if no `=` is present (bare attribute).
261: fn extract_attribute_value(attr_node: Node, source: &str) -> Option<String> {
262:     let mut found_eq = false;
263:     let mut cursor = attr_node.walk();
264: 
265:     for child in attr_node.children(&mut cursor) {
266:         let kind = child.kind();
267:         let text = node_text(child, source);
268: 
269:         if text == "=" {
270:             found_eq = true;
271:             continue;
272:         }
273: 
274:         if found_eq && kind != "=" {
275:             // Capture the first meaningful token after `=` as the value.
276:             return Some(text.trim().to_string());
277:         }
278:     }
279: 
280:     None
281: }
282: 
283: /// Find the first child of a node with the given kind.
284: fn find_first_child_of_kind<'a>(node: Node<'a>, kind: &str) -> Option<Node<'a>> {
285:     let child_count = node.child_count();
286:     for i in 0..child_count {
287:         if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
288:             if child.kind() == kind {
289:                 return Some(child);
290:             }
291:         }
292:     }
293:     None
294: }
295: 
296: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
297: // Function extraction
298: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
299: 
300: /// Build the full function name, including `set.` or `get.` prefix if present.
301: ///
302: /// In tree-sitter-matlab, `function set.Value(...)` produces:
303: /// - a child node with kind `set.`
304: /// - the `name` field pointing to the `identifier` node `Value`
305: ///
306: /// This function checks for that prefix and prepends it to the base name.
307: fn build_function_name(func_node: Node, source: &str) -> Option<String> {
308:     let name_node = func_node.child_by_field_name("name")?;
309:     let base_name = node_text(name_node, source);
310: 
311:     // Check for `set.` or `get.` prefix child.
312:     let child_count = func_node.child_count();
313:     for i in 0..child_count {
314:         if let Some(child) = func_node.child(i) {
315:             let kind = child.kind();
316:             if kind == "set." || kind == "get." {
317:                 return Some(format!("{}{}", kind, base_name));
318:             }
319:         }
320:     }
321: 
322:     Some(base_name.to_string())
323: }
324: 
325: /// Extract metadata from a `function_definition` node.
326: fn extract_function_meta(
327:     node: Node,
328:     source: &str,
329:     class_name: Option<&str>,
330:     is_method: bool,
331:     method_attributes: &[AttributeMeta],
332:     is_abstract: bool,
333: ) -> Option<FunctionMeta> {
334:     let name = build_function_name(node, source)?;
335: 
336:     let inputs = extract_function_inputs(node, source);
337:     let outputs = extract_function_outputs(node, source);
338: 
339:     let is_constructor = class_name.is_some_and(|cn| cn == name);
340:     let is_setter = name.starts_with("set.");
341:     let is_getter = name.starts_with("get.");
342: 
343:     let (has_arguments_block, argument_validations) = extract_arguments_blocks(node, source);
344: 
345:     Some(FunctionMeta {
346:         name,
347:         inputs,
348:         outputs,
349:         is_constructor,
350:         is_setter,
351:         is_getter,
352:         has_arguments_block,
353:         argument_validations,
354:         byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
355:         line: node.start_position().row + 1,
356:         end_line: node.end_position().row + 1,
357:         is_method,
358:         is_abstract,
359:         method_attributes: method_attributes.to_vec(),
360:     })
361: }
362: 
363: /// Extract a `function_signature` (abstract method stub with no body).
364: fn extract_function_signature(
365:     node: Node,
366:     source: &str,
367:     class_name: Option<&str>,
368:     method_attributes: &[AttributeMeta],
369: ) -> Option<FunctionMeta> {
370:     let name = build_function_name(node, source)?;
371: 
372:     let inputs = extract_function_inputs(node, source);
373:     let outputs = extract_function_outputs(node, source);
374: 
375:     let is_constructor = class_name.is_some_and(|cn| cn == name);
376:     let is_setter = name.starts_with("set.");
377:     let is_getter = name.starts_with("get.");
378: 
379:     Some(FunctionMeta {
380:         name,
381:         inputs,
382:         outputs,
383:         is_constructor,
384:         is_setter,
385:         is_getter,
386:         has_arguments_block: false,
387:         argument_validations: Vec::new(),
388:         byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
389:         line: node.start_position().row + 1,
390:         end_line: node.end_position().row + 1,
391:         is_method: true,
392:         is_abstract: true,
393:         method_attributes: method_attributes.to_vec(),
394:     })
395: }
396: 
397: /// Extract input argument names from a function definition.
398: fn extract_function_inputs(func_node: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<String> {
399:     let mut names = Vec::new();
400:     let mut cursor = func_node.walk();
401: 
402:     for child in func_node.children(&mut cursor) {
403:         if child.kind() == "function_arguments" {
404:             let mut inner = child.walk();
405:             for param in child.children(&mut inner) {
406:                 match param.kind() {
407:                     "identifier" => {
408:                         names.push(node_text(param, source).to_string());
409:                     }
410:                     "ignored_argument" => {
411:                         names.push("~".to_string());
412:                     }
413:                     _ => {}
414:                 }
415:             }
416:             break;
417:         }
418:     }
419: 
420:     names
421: }
422: 
423: /// Extract output argument names from a function definition.
424: fn extract_function_outputs(func_node: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<String> {
425:     let mut names = Vec::new();
426:     let mut cursor = func_node.walk();
427: 
428:     for child in func_node.children(&mut cursor) {
429:         if child.kind() == "function_output" {
430:             let mut inner = child.walk();
431:             for out_child in child.children(&mut inner) {
432:                 match out_child.kind() {
433:                     "identifier" => {
434:                         names.push(node_text(out_child, source).to_string());
435:                     }
436:                     "ignored_argument" => {
437:                         names.push("~".to_string());
438:                     }
439:                     "multioutput_variable" => {
440:                         let mut mv_cursor = out_child.walk();
441:                         for mv_child in out_child.children(&mut mv_cursor) {
442:                             match mv_child.kind() {
443:                                 "identifier" => {
444:                                     names.push(node_text(mv_child, source).to_string());
445:                                 }
446:                                 "ignored_argument" => {
447:                                     names.push("~".to_string());
448:                                 }
449:                                 _ => {}
450:                             }
451:                         }
452:                     }
453:                     _ => {}
454:                 }
455:             }
456:             break;
457:         }
458:     }
459: 
460:     names
461: }

463: /// Extract `arguments` validation blocks from within a function definition.
464: ///
465: /// Returns `(has_arguments_block, validations)`.
466: fn extract_arguments_blocks(func_node: Node, source: &str) -> (bool, Vec<ArgValidation>) {
467:     let mut validations = Vec::new();
468:     let mut found = false;
469: 
470:     let mut cursor = func_node.walk();
471:     for child in func_node.children(&mut cursor) {
472:         if child.kind() == "arguments_statement" {
473:             found = true;
474:             // Each `property` child inside the arguments block describes one argument.
475:             let mut inner = child.walk();
476:             for arg_child in child.children(&mut inner) {
477:                 if arg_child.kind() == "property" {
478:                     if let Some(validation) = extract_arg_validation(arg_child, source) {
479:                         validations.push(validation);
480:                     }
481:                 }
482:             }
483:         }
484:     }
485: 
486:     (found, validations)
487: }
488: 
489: /// Extract a single argument validation entry from a `property` node inside
490: /// an `arguments` block.
491: fn extract_arg_validation(prop_node: Node, source: &str) -> Option<ArgValidation> {
492:     let name = prop_node
493:         .child_by_field_name("name")
494:         .or_else(|| find_first_child_of_kind(prop_node, "identifier"))
495:         .map(|n| node_text(n, source).to_string())?;
496: 
497:     let dimensions = find_first_child_of_kind(prop_node, "dimensions")
498:         .map(|n| node_text(n, source).to_string());
499: 
500:     // Type constraint: bare identifier after dimensions (not the name).
501:     let type_constraint = extract_type_constraint(prop_node, source, &name);
502: 
503:     let validators = find_first_child_of_kind(prop_node, "validation_functions")
504:         .map(|vf| {
505:             let mut v = Vec::new();
506:             let mut vc = vf.walk();
507:             for vchild in vf.children(&mut vc) {
508:                 if vchild.kind() == "identifier" {
509:                     v.push(node_text(vchild, source).to_string());
510:                 }
511:             }
512:             v
513:         })
514:         .unwrap_or_default();
515: 
516:     let default_value = find_first_child_of_kind(prop_node, "default_value")
517:         .map(|dv| {
518:             // The actual expression is the child(ren) after `=`.
519:             // Use the full text, trimming the leading `=` if present.
520:             let text = node_text(dv, source).trim().to_string();
521:             let text = text.strip_prefix('=').unwrap_or(&text).trim().to_string();
522:             text
523:         });
524: 
525:     Some(ArgValidation {
526:         name,
527:         dimensions,
528:         type_constraint,
529:         validators,
530:         default_value,
531:     })
532: }
533: 
534: /// Extract the type constraint from a property node.
535: ///
536: /// In MATLAB, the property syntax is: `name (dims) type {validators} = default`.
537: /// The type is a bare identifier (or `property_name` for dotted names)
538: /// that appears after dimensions but before validation_functions/default_value.
539: fn extract_type_constraint(prop_node: Node, source: &str, prop_name: &str) -> Option<String> {
540:     let mut cursor = prop_node.walk();
541:     let mut past_name = false;
542:     let mut past_dims = false;
543: 
544:     for child in prop_node.children(&mut cursor) {
545:         let kind = child.kind();
546: 
547:         // Skip the name identifier.
548:         if !past_name {
549:             if kind == "identifier" || kind == "property_name" {
550:                 let text = node_text(child, source);
551:                 if text == prop_name {
552:                     past_name = true;
553:                     continue;
554:                 }
555:             }
556:             continue;
557:         }
558: 
559:         // Skip dimensions.
560:         if kind == "dimensions" {
561:             past_dims = true;
562:             continue;
563:         }
564: 
565:         // If we haven't seen dimensions yet and we encounter an identifier,
566:         // it could still be the type (dimensions are optional).
567:         if !past_dims && kind == "dimensions" {
568:             continue;
569:         }
570: 
571:         // The type constraint is the first identifier/property_name after
572:         // the property name (and optional dimensions).
573:         if kind == "identifier" || kind == "property_name" {
574:             return Some(node_text(child, source).to_string());
575:         }
576: 
577:         // If we hit validation_functions or default_value, no type was specified.
578:         if kind == "validation_functions" || kind == "default_value" || kind == "=" {
579:             return None;
580:         }
581:     }
582: 
583:     None
584: }

587: // Property extraction
588: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
