590: /// Extract property metadata from a `property` node inside a `properties` block.
591: fn extract_property_meta(prop_node: Node, source: &str) -> Option<PropertyMeta> {
592:     let name = prop_node
593:         .child_by_field_name("name")
594:         .or_else(|| find_first_child_of_kind(prop_node, "identifier"))
595:         .map(|n| node_text(n, source).to_string())?;
596: 
597:     let dimensions = find_first_child_of_kind(prop_node, "dimensions")
598:         .map(|n| node_text(n, source).to_string());
599: 
600:     let type_constraint = extract_type_constraint(prop_node, source, &name);
601: 
602:     let validators = find_first_child_of_kind(prop_node, "validation_functions")
603:         .map(|vf| {
604:             let mut v = Vec::new();
605:             let mut vc = vf.walk();
606:             for vchild in vf.children(&mut vc) {
607:                 if vchild.kind() == "identifier" {
608:                     v.push(node_text(vchild, source).to_string());
609:                 }
610:             }
611:             v
612:         })
613:         .unwrap_or_default();
614: 
615:     let default_value_node = find_first_child_of_kind(prop_node, "default_value");
616:     let has_default = default_value_node.is_some();
617:     let default_value = default_value_node.map(|dv| {
618:         let text = node_text(dv, source).trim().to_string();
619:         let text = text.strip_prefix('=').unwrap_or(&text).trim().to_string();
620:         text
621:     });
622: 
623:     Some(PropertyMeta {
624:         name,
625:         dimensions,
626:         type_constraint,
627:         validators,
628:         default_value,
629:         has_default,
630:         byte_range: prop_node.start_byte()..prop_node.end_byte(),
631:         line: prop_node.start_position().row + 1,
632:     })
633: }

635: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
636: // Class extraction
637: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
638: 
639: /// Extract class metadata from a `class_definition` node.
640: fn extract_class_meta(class_node: Node, source: &str) -> Option<ClassMeta> {
641:     let name_node = class_node.child_by_field_name("name")?;
642:     let class_name = node_text(name_node, source).to_string();
643: 
644:     // Superclasses.
645:     let superclasses = find_first_child_of_kind(class_node, "superclasses")
646:         .map(|sc| {
647:             let mut names = Vec::new();
648:             let mut cursor = sc.walk();
649:             for child in sc.children(&mut cursor) {
650:                 match child.kind() {
651:                     "identifier" | "property_name" => {
652:                         names.push(node_text(child, source).to_string());
653:                     }
654:                     _ => {}
655:                 }
656:             }
657:             names
658:         })
659:         .unwrap_or_default();
660: 
661:     // Class-level attributes.
662:     let attributes = find_first_child_of_kind(class_node, "attributes")
663:         .map(|a| extract_attributes(a, source))
664:         .unwrap_or_default();
665: 
666:     // Collect section blocks.
667:     let mut properties_blocks = Vec::new();
668:     let mut methods_blocks = Vec::new();
669:     let mut events_blocks = Vec::new();
670:     let mut enumeration_blocks = Vec::new();
671: 
672:     let mut cursor = class_node.walk();
673:     for child in class_node.children(&mut cursor) {
674:         match child.kind() {
675:             "properties" => {
676:                 properties_blocks.push(extract_properties_block(child, source));
677:             }
678:             "methods" => {
679:                 methods_blocks.push(extract_methods_block(child, source, &class_name));
680:             }
681:             "events" => {
682:                 events_blocks.push(extract_events_block(child, source));
683:             }
684:             "enumeration" => {
685:                 enumeration_blocks.push(extract_enumeration_block(child, source));
686:             }
687:             _ => {}
688:         }
689:     }
690: 
691:     Some(ClassMeta {
692:         name: class_name,
693:         superclasses,
694:         attributes,
695:         properties_blocks,
696:         methods_blocks,
697:         events_blocks,
698:         enumeration_blocks,
699:         byte_range: class_node.start_byte()..class_node.end_byte(),
700:         line: class_node.start_position().row + 1,
701:     })
702: }
703: 
704: /// Extract a `properties ... end` block.
705: fn extract_properties_block(props_node: Node, source: &str) -> PropertiesBlockMeta {
706:     let attributes = find_first_child_of_kind(props_node, "attributes")
707:         .map(|a| extract_attributes(a, source))
708:         .unwrap_or_default();
709: 
710:     let mut properties = Vec::new();
711:     let mut cursor = props_node.walk();
712:     for child in props_node.children(&mut cursor) {
713:         if child.kind() == "property" {
714:             if let Some(pm) = extract_property_meta(child, source) {
715:                 properties.push(pm);
716:             }
717:         }
718:     }
719: 
720:     PropertiesBlockMeta {
721:         attributes,
722:         properties,
723:     }
724: }
725: 
726: /// Extract a `methods ... end` block.
727: fn extract_methods_block(methods_node: Node, source: &str, class_name: &str) -> MethodsBlockMeta {
728:     let block_attributes = find_first_child_of_kind(methods_node, "attributes")
729:         .map(|a| extract_attributes(a, source))
730:         .unwrap_or_default();
731: 
732:     let mut methods = Vec::new();
733:     let mut cursor = methods_node.walk();
734:     for child in methods_node.children(&mut cursor) {
735:         match child.kind() {
736:             "function_definition" => {
737:                 if let Some(fm) = extract_function_meta(
738:                     child,
739:                     source,
740:                     Some(class_name),
741:                     true,
742:                     &block_attributes,
743:                     false,
744:                 ) {
745:                     methods.push(fm);
746:                 }
747:             }
748:             "function_signature" => {
749:                 if let Some(fm) =
750:                     extract_function_signature(child, source, Some(class_name), &block_attributes)
751:                 {
752:                     methods.push(fm);
753:                 }
754:             }
755:             _ => {}
756:         }
757:     }
758: 
759:     MethodsBlockMeta {
760:         attributes: block_attributes,
761:         methods,
762:     }
763: }
764: 
765: /// Extract an `events ... end` block.
766: fn extract_events_block(events_node: Node, source: &str) -> EventsBlockMeta {
767:     let attributes = find_first_child_of_kind(events_node, "attributes")
768:         .map(|a| extract_attributes(a, source))
769:         .unwrap_or_default();
770: 
771:     let mut events = Vec::new();
772:     let mut cursor = events_node.walk();
773:     for child in events_node.children(&mut cursor) {
774:         if child.kind() == "identifier" {
775:             events.push(node_text(child, source).to_string());
776:         }
777:     }
778: 
779:     EventsBlockMeta { attributes, events }
780: }
781: 
782: /// Extract an `enumeration ... end` block.
783: fn extract_enumeration_block(enum_node: Node, source: &str) -> EnumerationBlockMeta {
784:     let mut members = Vec::new();
785:     let mut cursor = enum_node.walk();
786:     for child in enum_node.children(&mut cursor) {
787:         if child.kind() == "enum" {
788:             // The enum member name is the first identifier child or "name" field.
789:             let name = child
790:                 .child_by_field_name("name")
791:                 .or_else(|| find_first_child_of_kind(child, "identifier"))
792:                 .map(|n| node_text(n, source).to_string());
793:             if let Some(n) = name {
794:                 members.push(n);
795:             }
796:         }
797:     }
798: 
799:     EnumerationBlockMeta { members }
800: }

802: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
803: // FileMeta construction
804: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
805: 
806: impl FileMeta {
807:     /// Extract metadata from a parsed tree and source text.
808:     ///
809:     /// Determines file type, extracts class/function/property metadata in a
810:     /// single walk of the top-level children.
811:     pub fn build(tree: &Tree, source: &str) -> Self {
812:         let root = tree.root_node();
813: 
814:         // ---- Determine file type -----------------------------------------
815:         let mut class_node: Option<Node> = None;
816:         let mut first_non_comment: Option<&str> = None;
817: 
818:         let mut cursor = root.walk();
819:         for child in root.children(&mut cursor) {
820:             let kind = child.kind();
821: 
822:             // Skip comments, line continuations, and whitespace nodes.
823:             if kind == "comment" || kind == "line_continuation" {
824:                 continue;
825:             }
826: 
827:             if kind == "class_definition" {
828:                 class_node = Some(child);
829:                 break; // class_definition found → ClassFile
830:             }
831: 
832:             if first_non_comment.is_none() {
833:                 first_non_comment = Some(kind);
834:             }
835:         }
836: 
837:         let file_type = if class_node.is_some() {
838:             FileType::ClassFile
839:         } else if first_non_comment == Some("function_definition") {
840:             FileType::FunctionFile
841:         } else {
842:             FileType::Script
843:         };
844: 
845:         // ---- Extract class metadata (if class file) ----------------------
846:         let class_meta = class_node.and_then(|cn| extract_class_meta(cn, source));
847:         let class_name = class_meta.as_ref().map(|c| c.name.as_str());
848: 
849:         // ---- Collect all functions from methods blocks (class file) ------
850:         let mut all_methods: Vec<FunctionMeta> = Vec::new();
851:         if let Some(ref cm) = class_meta {
852:             for mb in &cm.methods_blocks {
853:                 all_methods.extend(mb.methods.iter().cloned());
854:             }
855:         }
856: 
857:         // ---- Collect top-level functions ---------------------------------
858:         let mut functions: Vec<FunctionMeta> = Vec::new();
859:         let mut local_functions: Vec<FunctionMeta> = Vec::new();
860:         let mut main_function_seen = false;
861: 
862:         let mut cursor2 = root.walk();
863:         for child in root.children(&mut cursor2) {
864:             if child.kind() != "function_definition" {
865:                 continue;
866:             }
867: 
868:             // In a class file, top-level function_definitions after the class
869:             // are local/helper functions.
870:             if file_type == FileType::ClassFile {
871:                 if let Some(fm) =
872:                     extract_function_meta(child, source, class_name, false, &[], false)
873:                 {
874:                     local_functions.push(fm);
875:                 }
876:                 continue;
877:             }
878: 
879:             // Function file: first is main, rest are local.
880:             if let Some(fm) =
881:                 extract_function_meta(child, source, class_name, false, &[], false)
882:             {
883:                 if !main_function_seen {
884:                     main_function_seen = true;
885:                     functions.push(fm);
886:                 } else {
887:                     local_functions.push(fm);
888:                 }
889:             }
890:         }
891: 
892:         // Combine class methods + top-level functions.
893:         let mut all_functions = all_methods;
894:         all_functions.extend(functions);
895: 
896:         FileMeta {
897:             file_type,
898:             class: class_meta,
899:             functions: all_functions,
900:             local_functions,
901:         }
902:     }
903: 
904:     // ---- Helper methods --------------------------------------------------
905: 
906:     /// Get the main function (first function in a function file).
907:     ///
908:     /// Returns `None` for class files and scripts.
909:     pub fn main_function(&self) -> Option<&FunctionMeta> {
910:         if self.file_type == FileType::FunctionFile {
911:             self.functions.first()
912:         } else {
913:             None
914:         }
915:     }
916: 
917:     /// Get all methods (from all methods blocks in a class).
918:     ///
919:     /// Returns an empty vec for non-class files.
920:     pub fn all_methods(&self) -> Vec<&FunctionMeta> {
921:         self.functions.iter().filter(|f| f.is_method).collect()
922:     }
923: 
924:     /// Get all properties (from all properties blocks in a class).
925:     ///
926:     /// Returns an empty vec for non-class files.
927:     pub fn all_properties(&self) -> Vec<&PropertyMeta> {
928:         self.class
929:             .as_ref()
930:             .map(|c| {
931:                 c.properties_blocks
932:                     .iter()
933:                     .flat_map(|pb| pb.properties.iter())
934:                     .collect()
935:             })
936:             .unwrap_or_default()
937:     }
938: 
939:     /// Check if a method name exists in any methods block.
940:     pub fn has_method(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
941:         self.functions.iter().any(|f| f.is_method && f.name == name)
942:     }
943: 
944:     /// Check if a property name exists in any properties block.
945:     pub fn has_property(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
946:         self.class
947:             .as_ref()
948:             .is_some_and(|c| {
949:                 c.properties_blocks
950:                     .iter()
951:                     .flat_map(|pb| pb.properties.iter())
952:                     .any(|p| p.name == name)
953:             })
954:     }
955: 
956:     /// Get the class name (if class file).
957:     pub fn class_name(&self) -> Option<&str> {
958:         self.class.as_ref().map(|c| c.name.as_str())
959:     }
960: }

962: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
963: // ClassMeta helper methods
964: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
965: 
966: impl ClassMeta {
967:     /// Check if the class has a specific attribute (by name, case-sensitive).
968:     pub fn has_attribute(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
969:         self.attributes.iter().any(|a| a.name == name)
970:     }
971: 
972:     /// Get the value of a specific class-level attribute.
973:     ///
974:     /// Returns `None` if the attribute is not present or has no value.
975:     pub fn attribute_value(&self, name: &str) -> Option<&str> {
976:         self.attributes
977:             .iter()
978:             .find(|a| a.name == name)
979:             .and_then(|a| a.value.as_deref())
980:     }
981: 
982:     /// Check if the class is `Sealed`.
983:     ///
984:     /// Returns `true` if the `Sealed` attribute is present and not negated.
985:     pub fn is_sealed(&self) -> bool {
986:         self.attributes
987:             .iter()
988:             .any(|a| a.name == "Sealed" && !a.negated)
989:     }
990: 
991:     /// Check if the class is `Abstract`.
992:     ///
993:     /// Returns `true` if the `Abstract` attribute is present and not negated.
994:     pub fn is_abstract(&self) -> bool {
995:         self.attributes
996:             .iter()
997:             .any(|a| a.name == "Abstract" && !a.negated)
998:     }
999: 
1000:     /// Check if the class inherits from `handle`.
1001:     pub fn is_handle(&self) -> bool {
1002:         self.superclasses.iter().any(|s| s == "handle")
1003:     }
1004: }

1672:                                 | "catch_clause"
1673:                         )

1675:                     .unwrap_or(false);

1704: impl LanguageSpecEngine {
1705:     /// FCONF: Local function name same as file name.
1706:     fn check_local_function_name_conflict(
1707:         &self,
1708:         meta: &FileMeta,
1709:         ctx: &FileContext,
1710:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
1711:     ) {
1712:         let file_stem = ctx
1713:             .file_path
1714:             .file_stem()
1715:             .and_then(|s| s.to_str())
1716:             .unwrap_or("");

1718:             return;
1719:         }
1720: 
1721:         for func in &meta.local_functions {
1722:             if func.name == file_stem {
1723:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
1724:                     rule_id: "FCONF",
1725:                     message: format!(
1726:                         "Local function '{}' has the same name as the file",
1727:                         func.name
1728:                     ),
1729:                     severity: Severity::Error,
1730:                     byte_range: func.byte_range.clone(),
1731:                     line: func.line,
1732:                     column: 1,
1733:                     fix: None,
1734:                 });
1735:             }
1736:         }
1737:     }
1738: }

5: # Rules Reference
6: 
7: ## Overview
8: 
9: mlt implements lint rules matching MATLAB's Code Analyzer checks for feature parity. Rules use the same check IDs as MATLAB (e.g., `NOSEMI`, `AGROW`, `naming.class.casing`) and are organized into categories.
10: 
11: ## Rule Table
12: 
13: | Rule ID | Category | Description | Default Severity | Auto-fix |
14: | ------- | -------- | ----------- | ---------------- | -------- |
15: | [NOSEMI](nosemi.md) | Formatting | Statement without trailing semicolon may produce unintended console output | Info | Yes |
16: | [MFAMB](mfamb.md) | Readability | Cannot determine whether name is a variable or function; assumes function | Info | No |
17: | [FLUDLR](fludlr.md) | Readability | Nested `flipud(fliplr(x))`/`fliplr(flipud(x))` should use `rot90(x, 2)` | Info | Yes |
18: | [STLOW](stlow.md) | Readability | Unnecessary UPPER/LOWER call in a comparison | Info | Yes |
19: | [COMNL](comnl.md) | Readability | Newline following comma acts as a row separator in a matrix; suggest semicolon or ellipsis | Info | Yes |
20: | [FVINR](fvinr.md) | Readability | For readability, add Input attribute to the input arguments block | Info | Yes |
21: | [NOFIL](nofil.md) | Incomplete Analysis | File not found | Error | No |
22: | [RDERR](rderr.md) | Incomplete Analysis | Unable to read file | Error | No |
23: | [QUIT](quit.md) | Incomplete Analysis | Code analysis did not complete; the analyzer encountered an internal error | Error | No |
24: | [NOPAR2](nopar2.md) | Syntax Errors | A `(` might be missing a closing `)`, causing invalid syntax at `(` on a line | Error | No |
25: | [EOLPAR](eolpar.md) | Syntax Errors | A `(` might be missing a closing `)`, causing invalid syntax at end of line | Error | No |
26: | [ENDPAR](endpar.md) | Syntax Errors | A `(` might be missing a closing `)`, causing invalid syntax at end of file | Error | No |
27: | [UNSET](unset.md) | Syntax Errors | Invalid use of operator on the left side of an assignment | Error | No |
28: | [LHROW](lhrow.md) | Syntax Errors | The left side of an assignment cannot have multiple rows (';') | Error | No |
29: | [RESWD](reswd.md) | Syntax Errors | Invalid use of a reserved word | Error | No |
30: | [SYNEND](synend.md) | Syntax Errors | Invalid use for END operator | Error | No |
31: | [MCPLD](mcpld.md) | Syntax Errors | Invalid property syntax | Error | No |
32: | [BADNOT](badnot.md) | Syntax Errors | Using ~ to ignore a value is not permitted in this context | Error | No |
33: | [BADNOTLHS](badnotlhs.md) | Syntax Errors | Invalid use of logical not operator (~) on left side of an assignment | Error | No |
34: | [BADCT](badct.md) | Syntax Errors | Unicode explicit directional formatting characters are not supported | Error | No |
35: | [ENDCT2](endct2.md) | Syntax Errors | An END might be missing after a block-opening keyword | Error | No |
36: | [ENDCT3](endct3.md) | Syntax Errors | An END might be missing before a block-opening keyword | Error | No |
37: | [ENDCT4](endct4.md) | Syntax Errors | A METHODS block or END might be missing before a function definition | Error | No |

39: | [DOUQT](douqt.md) | Syntax Errors | A double quoted string is unterminated | Error | No |
40: | [INBLK](inblk.md) | Syntax Errors | A block comment is unterminated at the end of the file | Error | No |

53: | [VTPOD](vtpod.md) | Syntax Errors | Specify validation in the following order: size, then class, then functions | Error | No |
54: 
55: ## Rule Categories
56: 
57: mlt organizes rules into the same categories as MATLAB's Code Analyzer:
58: 
59: | Category | Config Key | Description |
60: | -------- | ---------- | ----------- |
61: | Incomplete Analysis | `incomplete-analysis` | Internal linter limits and analysis failures |
62: | Syntax Errors | `syntax-errors` | Parser-level syntax validation |
63: | Language Specification | `language-specification` | Language constraint violations |
64: | Bugs | `bugs` | Likely bugs and logic errors |
65: | Custom Checks | `custom-checks` | Configurable code complexity/style metrics |
66: | Naming | `naming` | Naming convention enforcement |
67: | Compatibility | `compatibility` | Deprecated/removed functions and APIs |
68: | Forward Compatibility | `forward-compatibility` | Forward compatibility issues |
69: | Good Practices | `good-practices` | Common best practices |
70: | Unset Variables | `unset-variables` | Variables that may not be defined before use |
71: | Unused Constructions | `unused-constructions` | Dead code and unused constructions |
72: | Suggested Improvements | `suggested-improvements` | Suggestions for improved code patterns |
73: | Readability | `readability` | Readability improvements |
74: | Formatting | `formatting` | Code formatting suggestions |
75: | Performance | `performance` | Performance improvement suggestions |
76: | Code Generation | `code-generation` | MATLAB Coder constraints |
77: | Fixed-Point | `fixed-point` | Fixed-point toolbox specific |
78: | Deployment | `deployment` | MATLAB Compiler deployment constraints |
79: | System Objects | `system-objects` | System object validation |
80: | Unsupported | `unsupported` | Unsupported features |
81: | Behavior Changes | `behavior-changes` | Behavior changes between MATLAB versions |
82: | Configuration Issues | `configuration-issues` | Configuration file validation |
83: 
84: ## Severity Levels
85: 
86: Rules are categorized into three severity levels:
87: 
88: ### Error
89: 
90: Critical issues that likely indicate bugs or broken code:
91: 
92: - Code that will fail at runtime
93: - Language specification violations
94: - Syntax errors
95: 
96: ### Warning
97: 
98: Issues that affect code quality:
99: 
100: - Common bug patterns
101: - Good practice violations
102: - Deprecated function usage
103: 
104: ### Info
105: 
106: Low-priority suggestions:
107: 
108: - Formatting preferences
109: - Performance improvement hints
110: - Readability suggestions
111: 
112: ### Configuring Severity
113: 
114: Override default severities in `.mlt.toml`:
115: 
116: ```toml
117: [lint.rules]
118: NOSEMI = "error"    # Upgrade from info to error
119: ```
120: 
121: Or in a full table:
122: 
123: ```toml
124: [lint.rules.NOSEMI]
125: severity = "error"
126: ignore_functions = ["disp", "fprintf"]
127: ```
128: 
129: ### Category-Level Configuration
130: 
131: Enable, disable, or override severity for entire categories:
132: 
133: ```toml
134: [lint.categories]
135: performance = "off"           # Disable all performance rules
136: compatibility = "warn"        # Override all compatibility rules to warning
137: formatting = "info"           # Set all formatting rules to info
138: ```
139: 
140: Per-rule configuration always takes precedence over category-level settings.
141: 
142: See [Configuration](configuration.md) for full details.
143: 
144: ## Enabling and Disabling Rules
145: 
146: All rules are enabled by default. Disable individual rules:
147: 
148: ```toml
149: [lint.rules]
150: NOSEMI = "off"
151: ```
152: 
153: Or disable entire categories:
154: 
155: ```toml
156: [lint.categories]
157: behavior-changes = "off"
158: ```
159: 
160: ## Auto-fix Support
161: 
162: Rules marked with "Yes" in the Auto-fix column provide automatic fixes. Run mlt with `--fix` to apply them:
163: 
164: ```bash
165: mlt --fix src/**/*.m
166: ```
167: 
168: Fixes are applied atomically per file. Overlapping fixes are detected and the conflicting fix is skipped with a warning.
169: 
170: ## Adding New Rules
171: 
172: mlt uses auto-registration via the `inventory` crate. To add a new rule:
173: 
174: 1. Create a new module in `crates/mlt_rules/src/` (e.g., `agrow.rs`)
175: 2. Implement the `Rule` trait with a `from_config` factory
176: 3. Add `inventory::submit!(crate::RuleRegistration::new("AGROW", Agrow::from_config));` at the bottom
177: 4. Add documentation in `docs/agrow.md`
178: 
179: No manual edits to `lib.rs` are needed beyond adding the `pub mod` declaration.
180: 
181: See the [repository](https://github.com/watermarkhu/mlt) for the full development guide.

2: fn dump(node: tree_sitter::Node, src: &str, depth: usize) {
3:     let indent = "  ".repeat(depth);
4:     let text = &src[node.start_byte()..node.end_byte()];
5:     let t = text.replace('\n', "\\n");
6:     let named = if node.is_named() { "" } else { " (anon)" };

9:     println!("{indent}{} {:?}{}{}", node.kind(), truncated, named, is_error);
10:     let mut cursor = node.walk();

1: # NOSEMI - Trailing Semicolon Missing
2: 
3: **Default severity:** Info
4: **Auto-fix:** Yes
5: **Category:** Formatting
6: **Can be disabled:** Yes
7: 
8: ## What this rule does
9: 
10: Flags MATLAB statements that do not end with a trailing semicolon (`;`). This applies to statements that produce a value — primarily assignments, function calls, and commands at the statement level.
11: 
12: ## Why this matters
13: 
14: - **Performance**: In loops, unsuppressed output causes significant slowdowns due to console I/O on every iteration
15: - **Noise**: Unintended console output clutters the Command Window, making it harder to find real output
16: - **Intent**: Without a semicolon, it's ambiguous whether the output was intentional (for debugging) or accidental
17: - **CI/CD**: Stray output in automated MATLAB scripts can pollute logs or interfere with output parsing
18: 
19: ## Examples
20: 
21: ### Correct
22: 
23: ```matlab
24: x = compute_value();
25: data = load('file.mat');
26: result = process(data);
27: 
28: % Intentional output (configure ignore_functions)
29: disp('Processing complete');
30: fprintf('Result: %d\n', result);
31: ```
32: 
33: ### Incorrect
34: 
35: ```matlab
36: x = compute_value()
37: data = load('file.mat')
38: result = process(data)
39: ```
40: 
41: ### Fixed
42: 
43: ```matlab
44: x = compute_value();
45: data = load('file.mat');
46: result = process(data);
47: ```
48: 
49: ## Configuration
50: 
51: ```toml title=".mlt.toml"
52: [lint.rules.NOSEMI]
53: severity = "info"
54: ignore_functions = ["disp", "fprintf", "warning", "error"]
55: ```
56: 
57: ### Parameters
58: 
59: | Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
60: | --------- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
61: | `severity` | string | `"info"` | Severity level (`"error"`, `"warn"`, `"info"`, `"off"`) |
62: | `ignore_functions` | array of strings | `[]` | Function names to exclude from this check |
63: 
64: ### `ignore_functions`
65: 
66: A list of function names that are commonly used for intentional console output. When a `function_call` or `command` statement calls one of these functions, the rule will not flag it even without a semicolon.
67: 
68: Common values:
69: 
70: ```toml
71: ignore_functions = [
72:     "disp",
73:     "fprintf",
74:     "warning",
75:     "error",
76:     "assert",
77:     "sprintf",  # usually assigned, but sometimes standalone
78: ]
79: ```
80: 
81: ## Automatic fixes
82: 
83: This rule inserts a semicolon (`;`) immediately after the end of the statement:
84: 
85: ```diff
86: - x = compute_value()
87: + x = compute_value();
88: ```
89: 
90: The fix is always safe — it suppresses output but does not change program behavior.
91: 
92: ## Target node types
93: 
94: This rule triggers on the following tree-sitter node types when they appear at statement level (direct children of `source_file` or `block`):
95: 
96: - `assignment` — Variable assignments (`a = expr`)
97: - `function_call` — Function calls used as statements (`foo(x)`)
98: - `command` — Command-syntax calls (`cd dir`, `help topic`)
99: 
100: Sub-expressions (e.g., `bar(1)` inside `x = foo(bar(1))`) are **not** flagged.
101: 
102: ## Related rules
103: 
104: - `NOCOMMA` — Missing comma between matrix elements
105: - `NO4LP` — Missing indentation for loop body

# LANGUAGE_SPEC_ENGINE - Language Specification Errors

**Default severity:** Error
**Auto-fix:** No
**Category:** Language Specification
**Can be disabled:** Yes

## What this rule does

The `LANGUAGE_SPEC_ENGINE` is a single file-level rule implementing MATLAB Code Analyzer checks for language specification constraint violations. It covers parfor restrictions (`PF*`), spmd restrictions (`SP*`), class/constructor rules, function validation, script-level checks, and the checks documented on this page.

This page documents the following sub-checks:

| Check ID | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| CTOINE | Use of constructed object as input to constructor is not supported |
| CTORO | Class constructors must be declared with at least one output argument |
| ERTXT | Specify an error message with the message identifier |
| MHERIT | Deriving from a built-in MATLAB class is not supported |
| NCHKOS | NARGINCHK does not return any values |
| SPBFN | Use of a workspace-access function inside an SPMD block |
| SPBRK | break/continue not fully contained in an SPMD block (subsumed by `SPRET`) |
| SPDEC | SPMD worker bounds must be nonnegative integers |
| SPDEC3 | SPMD can only specify lower and upper worker bounds |
| SPEVC | EVALIN/ASSIGNIN('caller') invalid inside an SPMD block |
| SPLD | Assign the output of LOAD to a variable in SPMD blocks |
| SPNF | Nested function call inside an SPMD block |
| SPSV | SAVE requires the '-fromstruct' option inside an SPMD block |
| SPWHOS | who/whos without '-file' is invalid inside an SPMD block |
| USESWNS | Variable must be explicitly defined before first use |
| WTXT | Specify a warning message with the message identifier |

## Why this matters

- **SPMD transparency**: Functions like `load`, `save`, `who`, `whos`, `eval`, `evalin`, and `assignin` access or modify the MATLAB workspace in ways that are not transparent to the SPMD runtime. Using them inside an `spmd` block can cause workers to behave inconsistently or fail.
- **Message identifiers**: `error` and `warning` calls that pass only a message identifier without a message body leave users with a bare ID instead of an actionable error text.
- **Constructor contracts**: MATLAB constructors must return the constructed object; passing a constructed object into a constructor is unsupported.
- **Script hygiene**: Scripts share the base workspace; a variable used before it is defined is likely a bug.

## Examples

### Correct

```matlab
function demo()
    spmd
        d = load('data.mat');                    % SPLD: assigned
        save('out.mat', '-fromstruct', s);       % SPSV: -fromstruct present
        who('-file', 'x.mat');                   % SPWHOS: -file present
    end
    error('MyTool:badInput', 'Bad input provided'); % ERTXT: has a message
    warning('plain message');                    % WTXT: plain message, no ID
end
```

### Incorrect

```matlab
function demo()
    spmd
        load('data.mat');              % SPLD
        save('out.mat');               % SPSV
        who;                           % SPWHOS
        evalin('caller', 'x');         % SPEVC
        eval('x');                     % SPBFN
    end
end

error('MyTool:badInput');              % ERTXT
warning('MyTool:badInput');            % WTXT
x = narginchk(1, 2);                   % NCHKOS
```

## Configuration

```toml title=".mlt.toml"
[lint.rules.LANGUAGE_SPEC_ENGINE]
severity = "error"
```

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --------- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `severity` | string | `"error"` | Severity level (`"error"`, `"warn"`, `"info"`, `"off"`) |

## Automatic fixes

None. All sub-checks report diagnostics only.

## Target node types

This rule is file-level (`has_file_check = true`) and analyzes the full parse tree:

- `function_call`, `command` — spmd transparency, error/warning message, and NCHKOS checks
- `spmd_statement` — worker bound checks (SPDEC, SPDEC3)
- `class_definition` — construction checks (CTOINE, CTORO, MHERIT)
- `source_file` — script-level checks (USESWNS)

## Notes

- `SPBRK` (break/continue whose enclosing loop is not fully contained in an SPMD block) is currently deferred: every `break`/`continue` directly inside an `spmd` block is already reported by `SPRET`.
- `USESWNS` overlaps with the Warning-severity `SUSENS` check from the unset-variables engine (`UNSET_VARIABLES_ENGINE`). This is the Error-severity language-specification variant; disable either engine via configuration if you prefer one over the other.
- `MHERIT` uses a conservative denylist of built-in classes (`double`, `single`, `int8`-`uint64`, `char`, `logical`, `cell`, `struct`).

## Related rules

- `SPRET`, `SPNST`, `SPGP` — other SPMD restrictions in this engine
- `SUSENS`, `SVNODEF` — unset-variables engine checks

- `function_call`, `command` — spmd transparency, error/warning message, and NCHKOS checks
- `spmd_statement` — worker bound checks (SPDEC, SPDEC3)
- `class_definition` — construction checks (CTOINE, CTORO, MHERIT), class attribute checks (MABSEAC, MCSWA, MTMAT, MTAGS3)

- `source_file` — script-level checks (USESWNS)

## Notes

- `SPBRK` (break/continue whose enclosing loop is not fully contained in an SPMD block) is currently deferred: every `break`/`continue` directly inside an `spmd` block is already reported by `SPRET`.
- `USESWNS` overlaps with the Warning-severity `SUSENS` check from the unset-variables engine (`UNSET_VARIABLES_ENGINE`). This is the Error-severity language-specification variant; disable either engine via configuration if you prefer one over the other.
- `MHERIT` uses a conservative denylist of built-in classes (`double`, `single`, `int8`-`uint64`, `char`, `logical`, `cell`, `struct`).
- `MCPSG` fires for setter/getter methods declared abstract, either as a bare `function_signature` or inside a `methods (Abstract)` block.
- `MCCSOP` fires only in the constructor; `MCSCN` fires in any method (including the constructor) that assigns to a `Constant` property.

1: # Language Specification - Function Validation Checks
2: 
3: **Default severity:** Error
4: **Auto-fix:** No
5: **Category:** Language Specification
6: **Can be disabled:** Yes
7: 
8: ## What these checks do
9: 
10: These checks validate `arguments` blocks and their interaction with the function signature, matching MATLAB Code Analyzer's function validation checks (FV\* family plus the size checks `TINVALDIM` and `TTOOFEWDIMS`).
11: 
12: The checks operate on three groups:
13: 
14: - **Structure** — block attributes, repeating blocks, output blocks, and class-name name-value arguments.
15: - **Ordering** — argument declaration order, duplicates, and consistency with the function line.
16: - **Validation** — validation function rules and size constraints.
17: 
18: ## Check IDs
19: 
20: ### Structure
21: 
22: | Check ID | Message |
23: | -------- | ------- |
24: | `FVDREP` | Multiple Repeating arguments blocks are not supported. |
25: | `FVIOA` | Specifying both 'Input' and 'Output' attributes on the same arguments block is not supported. |
26: | `FVREPO` | Repeating input arguments block containing varargin must not have other arguments. |
27: | `FVVREP` | varargin can only be used inside repeating input arguments block. |
28: | `FVOVREP` | Output argument varargout can only be used inside a Repeating output arguments block. |
29: | `FVNREP` | Name-value arguments are not supported in a Repeating arguments block. |
30: | `FVREPD` | Default values are not supported in a Repeating arguments block. |
31: | `FVOOD` | Specifying a default value for an output argument is not supported. |
32: | `FVOOI` | Use of ignored arguments in output arguments block is not supported. |
33: | `FVOON` | Using name-value argument as output argument is not supported. |
34: | `FVORM` | Declaring multiple repeating output arguments is not supported. |
35: | `FVOBI` | Declare all input argument blocks before all output arguments blocks. |
36: | `FVATF` | Attribute values in arguments blocks must be logical constants. |
37: | `FVMCL` | Specifying multiple name-value structures using .? syntax and a class name is not supported. |
38: | `FVNDE` | When specifying name-value arguments using a class name, it is illegal to specify default values for the arguments. |
39: | `FVNVL` | When specifying name-value arguments using a class name, it is illegal to specify validation for the arguments. |
40: 
41: ### Ordering and consistency
42: 
43: | Check ID | Message |
44: | -------- | ------- |
45: | `FVORDI` | Ignored input arguments are not allowed after a Repeating arguments block or name-value arguments. |
46: | `FVORDN` | Positional arguments must be defined before name-value arguments. |
47: | `FVORDP` | Positional arguments must be defined in the following order: required, optional, and repeating. |
48: | `FVORDO` | Repeating output arguments must be defined after required output arguments. |
49: | `FVAPN` | Move name-value arguments that use the name=value syntax to the end of the argument list. |
50: | `FVDAN` | Using the same name as both a name-value argument structure and as a positional argument is not supported. |
51: | `FVDAP` | Positional argument can only be declared once. |
52: | `FVDNF` | Name-value argument can only be declared once. |
53: | `FVSOR` | Input arguments block declarations and the function line must contain the same input arguments in the same order, including ignored arguments. |
54: | `FVSORO` | Output arguments block declarations and the function line must contain the same output arguments in the same order. |
55: | `FVNIV` | This variable is not an input to the function and cannot be used in an arguments block. |
56: | `FVIDV` | Specifying validation or default value for ignored arguments is not supported. |
57: 
58: ### Validation functions and size
59: 
60: | Check ID | Message |
61: | -------- | ------- |
62: | `FVVIN` | Validation function must use the argument as an input. |
63: | `FVVCON` | For input arguments, validation functions must only use previously declared positional arguments, the argument being validated, or literals. |
64: | `FVOCON` | For output arguments, validation functions must only use the argument being validated or literals. |
65: | `FVUBD` | Argument is referenced before it is declared in the arguments block. |
66: | `FVOND` | Use of name-value arguments in default values is not supported. |
67: | `FVONV` | Use of name-value arguments without dotted name in the validation is not supported. |
68: | `FVBTN` | Use of this function is not supported in arguments blocks. |
69: | `FVNSC` | Use of nested functions is not supported in arguments blocks. |
70: | `TINVALDIM` | Each dimension must be a nonnegative integer number or a colon. |
71: | `TTOOFEWDIMS` | Specify at least two dimensions for size. |
72: 
73: ## Why these checks matter
74: 
75: - **Arguments blocks** are the primary mechanism for input/output validation in modern MATLAB; malformed blocks cause runtime errors at the call site.
76: - **Declaration order** rules exist because MATLAB resolves positional, optional, repeating, and name-value arguments left-to-right; violations are rejected by the interpreter.
77: - **Validation function restrictions** (using only the argument, previously declared positionals, and literals) keep validation deterministic and side-effect free.
78: - **Size constraint checks** catch dimension declarations that can never match a concrete array.
79: 
80: ## Examples
81: 
82: ### Correct
83: 
84: ```matlab
85: function y = f(a, b, opts)
86:     arguments
87:         a (1,1) double
88:         b = 3
89:         opts.Name {mustBeReal}
90:     end
91:     y = a + b;
92: end
93: 
94: function [out, varargout] = g(x)
95:     arguments
96:         x (1,:) double {mustBeReal}
97:     end
98:     arguments (Output)
99:         out (1,1) double
100:     end
101:     arguments (Repeating)
102:         varargout
103:     end
104: end
105: ```
106: 
107: ### Incorrect
108: 
109: ```matlab
110: function y = f(a, b)
111:     arguments
112:         b = 3                 % FVORDP: optional before required
113:         a (1,1) double
114:         opts.Name = 'x'       % FVORDN: name-value after positional (also FVAPN)
115:     end
116:     y = a;
117: end
118: 
119: function [y] = g(x)
120:     arguments (Output)
121:         y (1,1) double = 5    % FVOOD: default value for an output
122:     end
123:     arguments (Input)
124:         x (1,1) double        % FVOBI: input block after output block
125:     end
126: end
127: ```
128: 
129: ## Configuration
130: 
131: These checks are part of the `LANGUAGE_SPEC_ENGINE` rule. Disable individual checks via `disabled_checks`:
132: 
133: ```toml title=".mlt.toml"
134: [lint.rules.LANGUAGE_SPEC_ENGINE]
135: disabled_checks = ["FVNIV", "TTOOFEWDIMS"]
136: ```
137: 
138: ### Parameters
139: 
140: | Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
141: | --------- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
142: | `disabled_checks` | array of strings | `[]` | Check IDs to disable within the language spec engine |
143: 
144: ## Automatic fixes
145: 
146: No automatic fixes are available for these checks.
147: 
148: ## Target node types
149: 
150: These checks run at the file level and inspect `function_definition` nodes and their `arguments_statement` children:
151: 
152: - `function_definition` — matched to extracted function metadata by byte range
153: - `arguments_statement` — an `arguments ... end` block, grouped with its attributes and arguments
154: - `attributes` — the block's `(Input)`, `(Output)`, `(Repeating)` attributes
155: - `property` — a single argument declaration
156: - `property_name` — a name-value argument declaration (`struct.field`)
157: - `class_property` — a `.?ClassName` name-value declaration
158: - `dimensions` — the size constraint
159: - `validation_functions` — the `{...}` validation function list
160: - `default_value` — the `= value` default expression
161: 
162: ## Related rules
163: 
164: - `FVNST` — Arguments blocks in nested functions
165: - `VTPOD` — Argument validation order (size, then class, then functions)
166: - `FVINR` — Add Input attribute to the input arguments block (readability)
167: 
168: ---
169: 
170: # Language Specification - Parfor Variable, Slicing, and Reduction Checks
171: 
172: These checks are also part of the `LANGUAGE_SPEC_ENGINE` rule. They validate parfor loop headers, banned functions, sliced output variables, and temporary/reduction variable classification, matching MATLAB Code Analyzer's parfor checks (PF\* family plus FPFORP and FWFORP).
173: 
174: ## Check IDs
175: 
176: ### Banned functions in parfor
177: 
178: | Check ID | Message |
179: | -------- | ------- |
180: | `PFEVC` | EVALIN('caller') and ASSIGNIN('caller') are invalid inside a PARFOR loop. |
181: | `PFINPT` | 'inputname' is not supported in parfor loops. |
182: | `PFNACK` | 'narginchk' and 'nargoutchk' cannot be used in parfor loops. |
183: | `PFNAIO` | 'nargin' and 'nargout' require a function argument in parfor loops. |
184: | `PFLD` | 'load' must assign to an output variable in parfor loops. |
185: | `PFSV` | SAVE cannot be called in a PARFOR loop without the '-fromstruct' option. |
186: | `FPFORP` | 'fprintf' is writing to a file opened with read permission only. |
187: | `FWFORP` | 'fwrite' is writing to a file opened with read permission only. |
188: | `PFCEL` | The function does not support cell arrays (argument N). |
189: 
190: ### Parfor loop variable restrictions
191: 
192: | Check ID | Message |
193: | -------- | ------- |
194: | `PFANSLP` | 'ans' is not supported as a parfor loop variable. |
195: | `PFANSNS` | 'ans' is not supported as a for loop variable in parfor loops. |
196: | `PFVSUB` | Indexing parfor loop variables is not supported in parfor loops. |
197: | `PFFSUB` | Indexing a nested for loop variable is not supported in parfor loops. |
198: | `PFMLTI` | The nested for loop variable must not be assigned other than by its for statement. |
199: | `PFRNG` | The range of a PARFOR statement must be increasing consecutive integers. |
200: 
201: ### Sliced variable rules
202: 
203: | Check ID | Message |
204: | -------- | ------- |
205: | `PFSLO` | Variable is indexed using the parfor loop variable, but it is not a valid sliced output variable. |
206: | `PFSLRD` | Invalid combination of sliced indexing and non-indexed reads of a sliced output variable. |
207: | `PFSLW` | Multiple sliced accesses must all use the same list of subscripts. |
208: | `PFANON` | Using a sliced output variable in an anonymous function is not supported in parfor loops. |
209: | `PFCTXT` | When indexing a sliced variable with a nested for loop variable, the sliced variable must be inside the for loop that defines its range. |
210: | `PFFRNG` | When indexing a sliced variable with a nested for loop variable, the range must be a row vector of positive constant numbers. |
211: 
212: ### Temporary and reduction variables
213: 
214: | Check ID | Message |
215: | -------- | ------- |
216: | `PFUTMP` | Temporary variable must be set inside the parfor loop before it is used. |
217: | `PFUTVR` | Variable may have been intended as a reduction variable, but is an uninitialized temporary. |
218: | `PFINCR` | Using different reduction functions with the same reduction variable is not supported in parfor loops. |
219: | `PFNAR` | Subtracting reduction variable from expressions is not supported in parfor loops. |
220: | `PFRFH` | The PARFOR reduction function must be a function name or a broadcast variable. |
221: | `PFUNK` | The PARFOR loop cannot run due to the way a variable is used. |
222: | `PFVARS` | Parfor loop contains too many variables. |
223: 
224: ## Why these checks matter
225: 
226: - **Parfor transparency** requires that every iteration be independent; functions that inspect the caller workspace (`evalin`/`assignin` with `'caller'`, `inputname`, `nargin`/`nargout`) or mutate the base workspace (`load`, `save`) break this model.
227: - **Sliced output variables** must be indexed by the parfor loop variable with a consistent subscript list; violations either serialize the loop, produce race conditions, or are rejected by the parallel pool.
228: - **Temporary variables** must be assigned before first use in every iteration; uninitialized temporaries are a common source of nondeterministic results.
229: - **Reduction variables** support a fixed set of associative/commutative functions; mixing operators or subtracting the reduction variable from an expression is rejected.
230: 
231: ## Examples
232: 
233: ### Correct
234: 
235: ```matlab
236: parfor i = 1:10
237:     x(i) = i;              % sliced output with consistent subscripts
238: end
239: 
240: s = 0;
241: parfor i = 1:10
242:     s = s + x(i);          % valid reduction (initialized before the loop)
243: end
244: ```
245: 
246: ### Incorrect
247: 
248: ```matlab
249: parfor i = 1:10
250:     evalin('caller', 'x'); % PFEVC
251:     load('data.mat');      % PFLD
252:     t = i * 2;
253:     y = t(i);              % PFSLO: t is a temporary, not a sliced output
254:     s = x(i) - s;          % PFNAR: subtracting reduction variable s
255: end
256: ```
257: 
258: ## Configuration
259: 
260: These checks are part of the `LANGUAGE_SPEC_ENGINE` rule. Disable individual checks via `disabled_checks`:
261: 
262: ```toml title=".mlt.toml"
263: [lint.rules.LANGUAGE_SPEC_ENGINE]
264: disabled_checks = ["PFEVC", "PFSLO"]
265: ```
266: 
267: ### Parameters
268: 
269: | Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
270: | --------- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
271: | `disabled_checks` | array of strings | `[]` | Check IDs to disable within the language spec engine |
272: 
273: ## Automatic fixes
274: 
275: No automatic fixes are available for these checks.
276: 
277: ## Target node types
278: 
279: These checks run at the file level and inspect the following tree-sitter nodes inside parfor bodies:
280: 
281: - `for_statement` — a `parfor` or nested `for` loop (distinguished by the `parfor`/`for` keyword child)
282: - `function_call` — banned functions, sliced/indexed accesses, and loop-variable indexing
283: - `assignment` — temporary, sliced, and reduction variable classification
284: - `command` — command-syntax `load`, `save`, `nargin`, `nargout`
285: - `identifier` — whole (non-indexed) reads
286: - `lambda` — anonymous functions referencing sliced output variables

# Language Specification - Class/Method Attribute, Constructor, and Superclass Checks

These checks are also part of the `LANGUAGE_SPEC_ENGINE` rule. They validate class and member attribute combinations, Constant and WeakHandle property usage, constructor/superclass call patterns, and method signature limits, matching MATLAB Code Analyzer's class checks (MC\* family plus `MTAGS3`, `MTMAT`, `MWKCL`, `MWKCT`, `MWKREF`).

## Check IDs

### Class attribute conflicts

| Check ID | Message |
| -------- | ------- |
| `MABSEAC` | Instance properties and methods are illegal in classes that are both Sealed and Abstract. |
| `MCSWA` | A sealed class cannot specify allowed subclasses. |
| `MTMAT` | Attribute can only be set once. |
| `MTAGS3` | Cannot use the Access attribute when using the SetAccess or GetAccess attribute. |

### Abstract/Sealed members

| Check ID | Message |
| -------- | ------- |
| `MABSEAM` | A method cannot be both Abstract and Sealed. |
| `MCMSP` | Private method cannot be Abstract. |
| `MCAPP` | Private property cannot be Abstract. |
| `MCGSA` | Method tries to set or get an abstract property. |
| `MCPSG` | Set or get method must be fully defined in the class definition file. |

### Constant and WeakHandle properties

| Check ID | Message |
| -------- | ------- |
| `MCCSOP` | Unable to modify Constant property. |
| `MCSCN` | Method tries to set a constant property. |
| `MWKCL` | A WeakHandle property must restrict its type using a class validation. |
| `MWKCT` | Specifying both WeakHandle and Constant attributes on the same property is not supported. |
| `MWKREF` | Specifying both WeakHandle and Dependent attributes is invalid. |

### Constructor/superclass calls

| Check ID | Message |
| -------- | ------- |
| `MCCBS` | A superclass constructor is being called, but the name is not a declared superclass name. |
| `MCCBU` | This superclass constructor is called after a use of the constructed object. |
| `MCCMC` | Constructor for superclass can only be called once. |
| `MCSCC` | To call the superclass constructor, the subclass constructor name must match the subclass name. |
| `MCSCF` | A superclass constructor must be assigned to the first constructor output argument. |
| `MCSCO` | A superclass constructor must be called using the first constructor output argument. |
| `MCSCT` | Superclass constructor call must not be conditionalized or be part of another expression. |
| `MCSMO` | Returning multiple outputs from a superclass object initialization is not supported. |
| `MCSCM` | To call a superclass method, the method name must match the subclass method name. |

### Method signatures

| Check ID | Message |
| -------- | ------- |
| `MCMIO` | Method has too many inputs or outputs. |
| `MCMTP` | TestParameterDefinition methods must be Static. |
| `MCPIN` | Unable to initialize class property to an instance of the class itself. |

## Why these checks matter

- **Mutually exclusive attributes** (`Sealed`+`Abstract`, `WeakHandle`+`Constant`, `WeakHandle`+`Dependent`, `Access`+`SetAccess`) describe states MATLAB cannot represent; the class is rejected at definition time.
- **Abstract members** must not be private or sealed, and set/get methods must be fully implemented — abstract accessors leave the property unusable.
- **Constant properties** cannot be reassigned after class load; assignments in the constructor or other methods are silently lost or error at runtime.
- **Superclass constructor calls** (`obj@SuperClass(...)`) must be the first operation, unconditional, assigned to the first output, and reference a declared superclass — violations produce undefined objects or runtime errors.
- **WeakHandle properties** need a class validation so MATLAB knows the concrete type the handle refers to.

## Examples

### Correct

```matlab
classdef GoodClass < Base
    properties (Constant)
        K = 42
    end
    properties (WeakHandle)
        ref SomeHandleClass
    end
    methods
        function obj = GoodClass()
            obj = obj@Base();
        end
    end
end
```

### Incorrect

```matlab
classdef (Sealed, Abstract) BadClass
    properties
        x                          % MABSEAC: instance property in Sealed+Abstract class
    end
    properties (WeakHandle, Constant)
        w                          % MWKCT
    end
    methods (Abstract, Sealed)
        function y = f(obj)        % MABSEAM
        end
    end
    methods
        function obj = BadClass()
            obj.y = 1;             % MCCBU: object used before superclass constructor
            if true
                obj = obj@Base();  % MCSCT: conditionalized superclass constructor
            end
            [obj, z] = obj@Base(); % MCCMC + MCSMO: second call with multiple outputs
        end
    end
end
```

## Configuration

These checks are part of the `LANGUAGE_SPEC_ENGINE` rule. Disable individual checks via `disabled_checks`:

```toml title=".mlt.toml"
[lint.rules.LANGUAGE_SPEC_ENGINE]
disabled_checks = ["MABSEAC", "MCSWA"]
```

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --------- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `disabled_checks` | array of strings | `[]` | Check IDs to disable within the language spec engine |

## Automatic fixes

No automatic fixes are available for these checks.

## Target node types

These checks run at the file level and use both `FileMeta`/`ClassMeta` metadata and raw tree walks:

- `class_definition` — class-level attribute checks (MABSEAC, MCSWA, MTMAT, MTAGS3)
- `properties` — property attribute checks (MCAPP, MCGSA, MWKCL, MWKCT, MWKREF, MCPIN)
- `methods` — method attribute checks (MABSEAM, MCMSP, MCPSG, MCMTP, MCMIO)
- `function_definition` — constructor/superclass call checks (MCCBS, MCCBU, MCCMC, MCSCF, MCSCN, MCSCO, MCSCT, MCSMO, MCSCC, MCSCM, MCCSOP)
- `assignment` — `obj.Prop = value` assignments to Constant properties

## Related rules

- `MCFIL`, `MCDIR`, `MCRED`, `MCCBD` — class file/name structure checks
- `MCS2I`, `MCS1O`, `MCG1I`, `MCG1O`, `MCSGP` — set/get method signature checks
- `CTOINE`, `CTORO`, `MHERIT` — constructor construction checks in this engine
